title.raw: 卷35 崔浩 Volume 35: Cui Hao

sentences.zh: 崔浩，字伯淵，清河人也，白馬公玄伯之長子。

translations.literal: Cui Hao, styled Boyuan, was a man of Qinghe, the eldest son of Duke of Baima Xuanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, whose style was Boyuan, came from Qinghe. He was the eldest son of Duke of Baima Xuanbo.

sentences.zh: 少好文學，博覽經史，玄象陰陽，百家之言，無不關綜，研精義理，時人莫及。

translations.literal: In youth he loved literature, read widely in classics and histories, celestial phenomena and yin-yang doctrine, and the hundred schools—none he did not connect and synthesize; he mastered principles of meaning, and none of his time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning. He read widely in the classics and histories, in astronomy and the yin-yang arts, and in the teachings of the hundred schools—there was none he did not weave together—and he penetrated their principles so deeply that no contemporary could rival him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為直郎。

translations.literal: At twenty he became Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was appointed Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天興中，給事祕書，轉著作郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era he served the Secretariat as attendant, then was transferred to Compiler in the Bureau of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing reign he served as an attendant in the Secretariat and was later transferred to Compiler in the Bureau of Writings.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其工書，常置左右。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor, because of his skill at calligraphy, often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his skill at calligraphy, Emperor Taizu often kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖季年，威嚴頗峻，宮省左右多以微過得罪，莫不逃隱，避目下之變，浩獨恭勤不怠，或終日不歸。

translations.literal: In the Taizu Emperor's final years his authority grew stern; many of those left and right in the palace establishment were punished for minor faults, and all fled and hid to avoid the changes of his glance—only Hao remained respectful and diligent without slackening, sometimes not returning home for whole days.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taizu's last years his authority grew severe. Many in the palace staff were punished for trifling faults, and all fled or hid to escape his sudden wrath—only Hao remained respectful and tireless in duty, sometimes not going home for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 太祖知之，輒命賜以御粥。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor learned of it, he would order imperial gruel bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he would order imperial gruel sent to him.

sentences.zh: 其砥直任時，不為窮通改節，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His upright adherence to duty through good and ill fortune without changing his integrity was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast integrity in office, never altering his principles whether in adversity or success, was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，拜博士祭酒，賜爵武城子，常授太宗經書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign he was appointed Libationer of the Erudites, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, and regularly instructed Taizong in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Taizong's reign he was appointed Libationer of the Erudites and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, and he regularly lectured the emperor on the classics.

sentences.zh: 每至郊祠，父子並乘軒軺，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Whenever suburban sacrifices came, father and son both rode in light carriages, and men of the time took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever suburban sacrifices were held, father and son rode together in light carriages—a sight others envied.

sentences.zh: 太宗好陰陽術數，聞浩說易及洪範五行，善之，因命浩筮吉凶，參觀天文，考定疑惑。

translations.literal: Taizong loved yin-yang arts and numerology; hearing Hao expound the Changes and the Five Elements of the Great Plan, he approved, and therefore ordered Hao to divine fortune and misfortune, consult the heavens, and resolve doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong delighted in yin-yang lore and numerology. When he heard Hao explain the Book of Changes and the Five Elements from the Great Plan, he was pleased and charged him to divine good and ill fortune, observe the heavens, and settle whatever was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 浩綜覈天人之際，舉其綱紀，諸所處決，多有應驗，恒與軍國大謀，甚為寵密。

translations.literal: Hao synthesized and verified the juncture of Heaven and man, grasped their guiding principles; in all his decisions many proved true, and he was constantly joined in the great plans of army and state, enjoying extreme favor and secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Hao mastered the connection between Heaven and human affairs and laid hold of their governing principles. Most of his judgments were borne out in fact, and he was constantly drawn into the weightiest military and state counsels, enjoying extraordinary trust and intimacy.

sentences.zh: 是時，有兔在後宮，驗問門官，無從得入。

translations.literal: At that time a hare appeared in the rear palace; when the gate officers were examined, none could have entered.
translations.idiomatic: About that time a hare was found in the inner palace. The gatekeepers were questioned, yet no one could have let it in.

sentences.zh: 太宗怪之，命浩推其咎徵。

translations.literal: Taizong found it strange and ordered Hao to deduce its omen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought it strange and ordered Hao to interpret the omen.

sentences.zh: 浩以為當有隣國貢嬪嬙者，善應也。

translations.literal: Hao held that there ought to be tribute of a consort or palace woman from a neighboring state—a favorable correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said that a neighboring state would soon present a consort or palace woman—a favorable sign.

sentences.zh: 明年，姚興果獻女。

translations.literal: The next year Yao Xing indeed presented a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yao Xing did in fact send a daughter as tribute.

sentences.zh: 神瑞二年，秋穀不登，太史令王亮、蘇垣因華陰公主等言讖書國家當治鄴，應大樂五十年，勸太宗遷都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui the autumn grain failed; the Director of Astronomy Wang Liang and Su Yuan, through Princess Huayin and others, cited prophetic writings that the state ought to rule from Ye and that great peace would last fifty years, urging Taizong to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenrui the autumn harvest failed. The Director of Astronomy Wang Liang and Su Yuan, speaking through Princess Huayin and others, cited prophetic texts saying the state should govern from Ye and would enjoy fifty years of great peace, and they urged Emperor Taizong to move the capital.

sentences.zh: 浩與特進周澹言於太宗曰：「今國家遷都於鄴，可救今年之飢，非長久之策也。

translations.literal: Hao and the Special Advancement Zhou Dan said to Taizong: "If the state now moves the capital to Ye, it may relieve this year's famine, but it is not a long-term policy.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and the Special Advancement Zhou Dan said to the emperor: "Moving the capital to Ye now might ease this year's famine, but it is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 東州之人，常謂國家居廣漠之地，民畜無算，號稱牛毛之眾。

translations.literal: The people of the eastern provinces constantly say the state dwells in vast desert lands, with people and livestock beyond counting, called a multitude like cattle hair.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the eastern provinces have long believed that our state sits in boundless steppe country, with people and herds beyond reckoning—a host as countless as hairs on cattle.

sentences.zh: 今留守舊都，分家南徙，恐不滿諸州之地。

translations.literal: Now if we leave the old capital and send households south in division, I fear they will not fill the lands of the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave the old capital and send families south in a mass migration, I fear they will not even fill the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 參居郡縣，處榛林之間，不便水土，疾疫死傷，情見事露，則百姓意沮。

translations.literal: Scattered among commanderies and counties, dwelling amid thorn scrub, unaccustomed to water and soil, with plague, death and injury—the facts once exposed will show the people's spirits broken.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered through the commanderies, living among scrub and woodland, unaccustomed to the climate, they will suffer plague and death. Once the truth becomes plain, the people's morale will collapse.

sentences.zh: 四方聞之，有輕侮之意，屈丐、蠕蠕必提挈而來，雲中、平城則有危殆之慮，阻隔恒代千里之險，雖欲救援，赴之甚難，如此則聲實俱損矣。

translations.literal: When the four quarters hear of it they will hold us in light contempt; the Qiyan and Rouran will surely link arms and come; Yunzhong and Pingcheng will face peril; blocked by the thousand-li barriers of Heng and Dai, though we wish to rescue, going will be very hard—thus both reputation and substance will be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters hear of it they will despise us. The Qiyan and Rouran will surely join forces and attack. Yunzhong and Pingcheng will be in danger. Cut off by the thousand-li barriers of Hengshan and Dai, rescue will be desperately slow—and both our prestige and our strength will suffer.

sentences.zh: 今居北方，假令山東有變，輕騎南出，燿威桑梓之中，誰知多少？

translations.literal: If we now dwell in the north, suppose Shandong has trouble—light cavalry ride south and display might in their native lands—who knows how many?
translations.idiomatic: If we remain in the north, then whenever trouble arises in the east a body of light cavalry can ride south and show our might in the heart of China—who can say how great that force might be?

sentences.zh: 百姓見之，望塵震服。

translations.literal: When the people see it, they will be shaken into submission at the sight of the dust.
translations.idiomatic: The common people, seeing them, will submit at the mere sight of their dust.

sentences.zh: 此是國家威制諸夏之長策也。

translations.literal: This is the state's long-term policy for awe and control over the various Xia.
translations.idiomatic: That is the state's enduring strategy for holding the Chinese realms in awe.

sentences.zh: 至春草生，乳酪將出，兼有菜果，足接來秋，若得中熟，事則濟矣。

translations.literal: When spring grass grows, dairy will come forth, and together with vegetables and fruit it will suffice to bridge to the coming autumn; if we get an average harvest, the matter will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: When spring grass grows there will be milk and cheese again, and with vegetables and fruit we can bridge to the next autumn. An ordinary harvest will see us through.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深然之，曰：「唯此二人，與朕意同。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply approved, saying: "Only these two men agree with my mind.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply convinced and said, "Only these two men share my view.

sentences.zh: 」復使中貴人問浩、澹曰：「今既糊口無以至來秋，來秋或復不熟，將如之何？

translations.literal: " He again sent a palace eunuch to ask Hao and Dan: "Now we barely have mouths to feed until next autumn; if next autumn again fails to ripen, what then shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: " He again sent a palace eunuch to ask Hao and Dan: "We can barely feed ourselves until next autumn. If next autumn's harvest fails again, what then?

sentences.zh: 」浩等對曰：「可簡窮下之戶，諸州就穀，若來秋無年，願更圖也。

translations.literal: " Hao and the others replied: "We may select the poorest households and send them to the various provinces for grain; if next autumn has no harvest, we beg to plan anew.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao and the others replied: "Select the poorest households and send them to the eastern provinces for grain. If next autumn fails again, we can devise another plan then.

sentences.zh: 但不可遷都。

translations.literal: Only we must not move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But we must not move the capital.

sentences.zh: 」太宗從之，於是分民詣山東三州食，出倉穀以稟之。

translations.literal: " Taizong followed this; thereupon the people were divided and sent to the three eastern provinces for food, and granary grain was issued to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed. The people were sent to the three eastern provinces for food, and grain from the state granaries was issued to sustain them.

sentences.zh: 來年遂大熟。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The following year brought a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 賜浩、澹妾各一人，御衣一襲，絹五十匹，綿五十斤。

translations.literal: Hao and Dan were each granted a concubine, one suit of imperial robes, fifty bolts of silk, and fifty jin of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Dan were each given a concubine, a suit of imperial robes, fifty bolts of silk, and fifty jin of cotton.

sentences.zh: 初，姚興死之前歲也，太史奏：熒惑在匏瓜星中，一夜忽然亡失，不知所在。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the year before Yao Xing's death, the Director of Astronomy reported: Mars was in the Gourd constellation; in one night it suddenly vanished, its whereabouts unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the year before Yao Xing died, the Director of Astronomy reported that Mars stood in the Gourd constellation, then vanished overnight with no one knowing where it had gone.

sentences.zh: 或謂下入危亡之國，將為童謠妖言，而後行其災禍。

translations.literal: Some said it had descended into a state facing peril and ruin, and would first produce children's songs and strange talk before bringing its calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Some said it had descended into a doomed state and would first stir up children's rhymes and wild rumors before the disaster struck.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，大驚，乃召諸碩儒十數人，令與史官求其所詣。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and was greatly alarmed; he summoned more than ten eminent scholars and ordered them with the historiographers to seek where it had gone.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he was deeply alarmed. He summoned more than ten leading scholars and ordered them, together with the court astronomers, to determine where the star had gone.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「案春秋左氏傳說神降于莘，其至之日，各以其物祭也。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "According to the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a spirit descended at Shen, on the day of its arrival each offered sacrifice with its proper object.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied: "The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals records that when a spirit descended at Shen, on the day of its arrival each kind of being offered sacrifice with its proper offering.

sentences.zh: 請以日辰推之，庚午之弘，辛未之朝，天有陰雲，熒惑之亡，當在此二日之內。

translations.literal: I beg to calculate by day and stem-branch: on the gengwu day at dusk, on the xinwei morning, the sky had dark clouds—the vanishing of Mars ought to fall within these two days.
translations.idiomatic: Let us reckon by the calendar: on the evening of gengwu and the morning of xinwei the sky was overcast. Mars must have vanished within those two days.

sentences.zh: 庚之與未，皆主於秦，辛為西夷。

translations.literal: Geng and wei both belong to Qin; xin is the western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Geng and wei both correspond to Qin; xin corresponds to the western barbarians.

sentences.zh: 今姚興據咸陽，是熒惑入秦矣。

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing now holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.

sentences.zh: 」諸人皆作色曰：「天上失星，人安能知其所詣，而妄說無徵之言。

translations.literal: " All changed color and said: "A star is lost in heaven—how can a man know where it has gone, and yet speak reckless words without proof."
translations.idiomatic: " The others flushed with anger and said, "When a star vanishes from the sky, how can any man know where it has gone? You speak recklessly without proof.

sentences.zh: 」浩笑而不應。

translations.literal: " Hao smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao only smiled and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 後八十餘日，熒惑果出於東井，留守盤遊，秦中大旱赤地，昆明池水竭，童謠訛言，國內諠擾。

translations.literal: After more than eighty days Mars indeed appeared in the Well constellation, lingering and roaming; within Qin there was great drought and bare red earth, the Kunming Pool dried up, children's songs and false reports spread, and the realm was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty days later Mars did appear in the Well constellation, lingering there. Qin suffered severe drought until the land was bare and red; the Kunming Pool ran dry; children's rhymes and wild rumors spread; the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 明年，姚興死，二子交兵，三年國滅。

translations.literal: The next year Yao Xing died; his two sons fought each other; in three years the state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yao Xing died. His two sons fought each other, and within three years the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 於是諸人皆服曰：「非所及也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon all submitted and said: "Not what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: Then all conceded: "We could never have matched that."

sentences.zh: 泰常元年，司馬德宗將劉裕伐姚泓，舟師自淮泗入清，欲泝河西上，假道於國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, Sima Dezong's general Liu Yu was about to attack Yao Hong; his fleet entered the Qing from the Huai and Si, intending to go up the Yellow River westward and seek passage through our state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang, Liu Yu, general of the Jin emperor Sima Dezong, prepared to attack Yao Hong. His fleet entered the Qing River from the Huai and Si, intending to ascend the Yellow River westward and request passage through our territory.

sentences.zh: 詔羣臣議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 外朝公卿咸曰：「函谷關號曰天險。

translations.literal: The outer-court nobles and ministers all said: "Hangu Pass is called heaven's barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The outer-court nobles and ministers all said: "Hangu Pass is called heaven's own barrier.

sentences.zh: 一人荷戈，萬夫不得進。

translations.literal: One man bearing a spear—ten thousand cannot advance.
translations.idiomatic: One man with a spear can hold off ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 裕舟船步兵，何能西入？

translations.literal: How can Yu's ships and infantry enter the west?
translations.idiomatic: How can Liu Yu's ships and foot soldiers force their way west?

sentences.zh: 脫我乘其後，還路甚難。

translations.literal: If by chance we strike from behind, his return road will be very hard.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike from behind, his retreat will be desperately difficult.

sentences.zh: 若北上河岸，其行為易。

translations.literal: If he goes north onto the river bank, his march will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: If he lands on the north bank, his march will be easy.

sentences.zh: 揚言伐姚，意或難測。

translations.literal: He proclaims an attack on Yao, but his intent may be hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: He claims to be attacking Yao, but his true intent may be hard to read.

sentences.zh: 假其水道，寇不可縱，宜先發軍斷河上流，勿令西過。

translations.literal: To lend him the water route—bandits must not be indulged; we ought first to send troops and block the upper river, not letting him pass west.
translations.idiomatic: We must not let an enemy use our waterways. We should send troops first to block the upper river and forbid him to pass westward.

sentences.zh: 」又議之內朝，咸同外計。

translations.literal: " When deliberated in the inner court, all agreed with the outer plan.
translations.idiomatic: " When the inner court debated the matter, all agreed with the outer court.

sentences.zh: 太宗將從之。

translations.literal: Taizong was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to accept this advice.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「此非上策。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This is not the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "This is not the best course.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之之徒擾其荊州，劉裕切齒來久。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi and his faction have troubled his Jing province; Liu Yu has gnashed his teeth for long.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi and his faction have ravaged Liu Yu's Jing province. Liu Yu has long burned for revenge.

sentences.zh: 今興死子劣，乘其危亡而伐之，臣觀其意，必欲入關。

translations.literal: Now Xing is dead and the son is weak; seizing their peril and ruin to attack—I observe his intent: he surely wishes to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing is dead and his son is weak. Liu Yu is striking while Qin is in peril. In my view his aim is certainly to enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 勁躁之人，不顧後患。

translations.literal: A fierce, impetuous man does not heed later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce and impetuous man does not count the cost.

sentences.zh: 今若塞其西路，裕必上岸北侵，如此則姚無事而我受敵。

translations.literal: If we now block his western route, Yu will surely go ashore and invade north—thus Yao will be unharmed while we bear the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If we block his western route now, Liu Yu will surely land on the north bank and invade us—Yao will be spared while we bear the attack.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕內寇，民食又乏，不可發軍。

translations.literal: Now the Rouran raid within, and the people's food is again scarce—we cannot send troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran are raiding within our borders and food is scarce again. We cannot deploy an army.

sentences.zh: 發軍赴南則北寇進擊，若其救北則東州復危。

translations.literal: Send troops south and the northern raiders will strike; if we rescue the north, the eastern provinces are again in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops south and the northern raiders advance. Rescue the north and the eastern provinces are endangered again.

sentences.zh: 未若假之水道，縱裕西入，然後興兵塞其東歸之路，所謂卞莊刺虎，兩得之勢也。

translations.literal: Better to lend him the water route, let Yu enter west, then raise troops and block his eastern return road—the so-called Bian Zhuang stabs the tiger, gaining advantage from both.
translations.idiomatic: Better to grant him the water route, let Liu Yu pass west, then raise troops to block his return east—the stratagem of Bian Zhuang stabbing the tiger, profiting from both sides.

sentences.zh: 使裕勝也，必德我假道之惠；

translations.literal: If Yu wins, he will surely be grateful for our lending the road;
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Yu wins, he will owe us for granting passage;

sentences.zh: 令姚氏勝也，亦不失救隣之名。

translations.literal: if the Yao clan wins, we still do not lose the name of aiding a neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: if the Yao prevail, we still keep the credit of aiding a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 縱使裕得關中，縣遠難守，彼不能守，終為我物。

translations.literal: Even if Yu gains Guanzhong, the districts are distant and hard to hold—he cannot hold them, and in the end they become our possession.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Liu Yu takes Guanzhong, the region is remote and he cannot hold it. In the end it will be ours.

sentences.zh: 今不勞兵馬，坐觀成敗，鬬兩虎而收長久之利，上策也。

translations.literal: Now without troubling troops and horses, sit and watch success and failure—set two tigers fighting and reap lasting profit: the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: Without moving our own forces we can watch the outcome, set two tigers against each other, and reap a lasting gain. That is the best policy.

sentences.zh: 夫為國之計，擇利而為之，豈顧婚姻，酬一女子之惠哉？

translations.literal: In planning for a state, one chooses profit and acts—how should one care for marriage alliance, repaying the favor of one woman's gift?
translations.idiomatic: Statecraft chooses profit and acts accordingly. Why should we honor a marriage tie or repay the gift of a single woman?

sentences.zh: 假令國家棄恒山以南，裕必不能發吳越之兵與官軍爭守河北也，居然可知。

translations.literal: Even if the state abandoned all south of Hengshan, Yu surely could not raise Wu-Yue troops to contend with our army for Hebei—it is plainly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we abandoned everything south of Hengshan, Liu Yu could not raise Wu and Yue troops to contest Hebei with our armies—that much is plain.

sentences.zh: 」議者猶曰：「裕西入函谷，則進退路窮，腹背受敵；

translations.literal: " The debaters still said: "If Yu enters Hangu westward, advance and retreat are cut off, attacked front and rear;
translations.idiomatic: " The debaters still objected: "If Liu Yu enters Hangu from the west, his advance and retreat are cut off and he will be attacked front and rear.

sentences.zh: 北上岸則姚軍必不出關助我。

translations.literal: if he goes ashore north, the Yao army will surely not leave the passes to aid us.
translations.idiomatic: If he lands on the north bank, the Yao army will surely not leave the passes to help us.

sentences.zh: 揚聲西行，意在北進，其勢然也。

translations.literal: He proclaims going west while his intent is to advance north—the trend is so.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaims a western march while intending to strike north—that is how the situation will unfold.

sentences.zh: 」太宗遂從羣議，遣長孫嵩發兵拒之，戰於畔城，為裕將朱超石所敗，師人多傷。

translations.literal: " Taizong then followed the assembly's counsel, sent Changgunsong to raise troops to resist; they fought at Pancheng and were defeated by Yu's general Zhu Chaoshi, many of the army wounded.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed the majority. He sent Changgunsong to block Liu Yu. At Pancheng they were defeated by Liu Yu's general Zhu Chaoshi, and many soldiers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，恨不用浩計。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and regretted not using Hao's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he regretted not having followed Hao's advice.

sentences.zh: 二年，司馬德宗齊郡太守王懿來降，上書陳計，稱劉裕在洛，勸國家以軍絕其後路，則裕軍可不戰而克。

translations.literal: In the second year, Sima Dezong's Administrator of Qi Commandery Wang Yi came to surrender, memorializing with a plan, saying Liu Yu was at Luoyang, urging the state to send troops and cut his rear route—then Yu's army could be taken without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Wang Yi, Administrator of Qi under the Jin emperor Sima Dezong, came over to us. In his memorial he said Liu Yu was at Luoyang and urged our state to cut off his retreat with an army, so that Liu Yu's forces could be destroyed without a battle.

sentences.zh: 書奏，太宗善之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, Taizong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and approved it.

sentences.zh: 會浩在前進講書傳，太宗問浩曰：「劉裕西伐，前軍已至潼關。

translations.literal: It happened that Hao was in the forward camp lecturing on the classics when Taizong asked Hao: "Liu Yu is campaigning west; his vanguard has already reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hao happened to be at the forward camp lecturing on the classics when the emperor asked him: "Liu Yu is campaigning westward. His vanguard has already reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 其事如何？

translations.literal: How stands the affair?
translations.idiomatic: How do matters stand?

sentences.zh: 以卿觀之，事得濟不？

translations.literal: In your view, can the affair succeed?
translations.idiomatic: In your view, will he succeed?

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「昔姚興好養虛名，而無實用。

translations.literal: " Hao replied: "Formerly Yao Xing loved to cultivate empty reputation without real utility.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied: "Yao Xing once cultivated empty reputation without real strength.

sentences.zh: 子泓又病，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: The son Hong is again ill; the masses rebel and kin depart.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong is ill again. His followers have deserted and his kin turned away.

sentences.zh: 裕乘其危，兵精將勇，以臣觀之，克之必矣。

translations.literal: Yu seizes their peril; troops are elite and generals brave—in my view he will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu strikes while Qin is in peril. His troops are elite and his commanders bold. In my view he is certain to prevail.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「劉裕武能何如慕容垂？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "How does Liu Yu's martial ability compare with Murong Chui?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked: "How does Liu Yu's military talent compare with Murong Chui's?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「裕勝。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Yu surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "Liu Yu is the greater.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「試言其狀。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "Try to describe how this is so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Explain how that is so.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「慕容垂乘父祖世君之資，生便尊貴，同類歸之，若夜蛾之赴火，少加倚仗，便足立功。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Murong Chui rode the resources of father and forebears as successive rulers; born already noble, his kindred came to him like night moths to flame—with slight reliance he sufficed for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "Murong Chui inherited the standing of fathers and grandfathers who had ruled for generations. Born to eminence, men flocked to him like moths to flame. With little effort he could win glory.

sentences.zh: 劉裕挺出寒微，不階尺土之資，不因一卒之用，奮臂大呼而夷滅桓玄，北擒慕容超，南摧盧循等，僭晉陵遲，遂執國命。

translations.literal: Liu Yu rose from cold obscurity, without a foot of land as resource, without the use of a single soldier—he flung up his arms and shouted, and extinguished Huan Xuan; north he captured Murong Chao, south he crushed Lu Xun and others; the usurping Jin lingered in decline, and he then grasped the nation's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rose from utter obscurity without an inch of land or a single soldier at his command. He raised his arm and cried out, destroyed Huan Xuan, captured Murong Chao in the north and crushed Lu Xun in the south. The usurping Jin court lingered in decay, and he seized the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 裕若平姚而還，必篡其主，其勢然也。

translations.literal: If Yu pacifies Yao and returns, he will surely usurp his lord—the trend is so.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Yu pacifies Qin and returns, he will surely supplant his sovereign. That is how the situation will unfold.

sentences.zh: 秦地戎夷混并，虎狼之國，裕亦不能守之。

translations.literal: The Qin lands mix Di and Yi; it is a country of tigers and wolves—Yu also cannot hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin region is a mingled land of barbarians, a country of tigers and wolves. Liu Yu cannot hold it either.

sentences.zh: 風俗不同，人情難變，欲行荊揚之化於三秦之地，譬無翼而欲飛，無足而欲走，不可得也。

translations.literal: Customs differ, human feelings are hard to change—wishing to enact Jing-Yang transformation in the land of Three Qin is like wishing to fly without wings or run without feet: it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Customs differ and hearts are slow to change. To impose the ways of Jing and Yang on the Three Qin is like trying to fly without wings or run without feet—it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 若留眾守之，必資於寇。

translations.literal: If he leaves a host to guard it, he must supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If he leaves troops to garrison the region, he will only feed our enemies.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：善人為邦百年，可以勝殘去殺。

translations.literal: Confucius said: If a good man governs a state for a hundred years, he can overcome cruelty and remove killing.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that if a good man ruled a state for a hundred years, he could overcome cruelty and abolish killing.

sentences.zh: 今以秦之難制，一二年間豈裕所能哉？

translations.literal: Now given Qin's difficulty to control, in one or two years how could Yu manage it?
translations.idiomatic: Given how hard Qin is to govern, how could Liu Yu master it in a year or two?

sentences.zh: 且可治戎束甲，息民備境，以待其歸，秦地亦當終為國有，可坐而守也。

translations.literal: Moreover we may govern the Rong, bind armor, rest the people and guard the borders, waiting for his return—Qin lands too should in the end become our state's possession; we may sit and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: We should instead ready our defenses, arm the frontier, rest the people, and guard the borders until he returns. Qin will ultimately be ours, and we can hold it without stirring.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「裕已入關，不能進退，我遣精騎南襲彭城、壽春，裕亦何能自立？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "Yu has entered the passes and cannot advance or retreat; if I send elite cavalry south to strike Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can Yu stand alone?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Liu Yu is inside the passes and cannot advance or retreat. If I send elite cavalry south against Pengcheng and Shouchun, how can he hold his position?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「今西北二寇未殄，陛下不可親御六師。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Now the two foes of the northwest are not destroyed; Your Majesty cannot personally lead the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "The two enemies in the northwest are not yet destroyed. Your Majesty cannot personally lead the main armies.

sentences.zh: 兵眾雖盛，而將無韓白。

translations.literal: Though the troops are numerous, there is no general like Han or Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces are numerous, but we have no commander equal to Han Xin or Bai Qi.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩有治國之用，無進取之能，非劉裕敵也。

translations.literal: Changgunsong has use for governing the state but not capacity for advance and seizure—he is no match for Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Changgunsong is fit to govern the state but lacks the drive for conquest. He is no match for Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 臣謂待之不晚。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that waiting is not late.
translations.idiomatic: I say there is no hurry to act.

sentences.zh: 」太宗笑曰：「卿量之已審矣。

translations.literal: " Taizong laughed and said: "Your measure of things is already thorough.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "You have judged the matter already with full clarity.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「臣嘗私論近世人物，不敢不上聞。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Your servant has privately discussed men of recent times and dares not withhold it from Your Majesty's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "I have privately formed opinions on men of recent times and dare not withhold them from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 若王猛之治國，苻堅之管仲也；

translations.literal: Wang Meng in governing the state was Fu Jian's Guan Zhong;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng in governing the state was to Fu Jian what Guan Zhong was to Duke Huan;

sentences.zh: 慕容玄恭之輔少主，慕容暐之霍光也；

translations.literal: Murong Xuanggong in assisting the young lord was Murong Wei's Huo Guang;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xuanggong in assisting the young ruler was to Murong Wei what Huo Guang was to Emperor Xuan;

sentences.zh: 劉裕之平逆亂，司馬德宗之曹操也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu in pacifying rebellion was Sima Dezong's Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu in quelling rebellion was to Sima Dezong what Cao Cao was to the Han emperor.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「卿謂先帝如何？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "What do you say of the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "What do you make of the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「小人管窺懸象，何能見玄穹之廣大。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "This petty man peeps through a tube at the hanging image—how can he see the vastness of the dark vault?
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "I am but a narrow observer—how could I take in the vastness of heaven?

sentences.zh: 雖然，太祖用漠北醇樸之人，南入中地，變風易俗，化洽四海，自與羲農齊列，臣豈能仰名。

translations.literal: Even so, the Taizu Emperor employed the pure and simple men of the northern desert, entered the central lands southward, changed customs and transformed practices, and his transforming influence reached the four seas—he ranks himself with Fuxi and Shennong; how could your servant presume to name him?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Taizu Emperor took the plain, honest men of the northern steppe, entered the central plains, and changed customs until his transforming influence reached the four seas. He stands with Fuxi and Shennong—how could I presume to name his stature?

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「屈丐何如？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "What of the Qiyan?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "What of the Qiyan chief?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「屈丐家國夷滅，一身孤寄，為姚氏封殖。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "The Qiyan chief's state and clan were destroyed and extinguished; he alone drifted in exile and was fostered by the Yao clan.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "The Qiyan chief's state and clan were destroyed. He drifted alone into exile and was sheltered and raised by the Yao.

sentences.zh: 不思樹黨強隣，報讎雪耻，乃結忿於蠕蠕，背德於姚興，撅竪小人，無大經略，正可殘暴，終為人所滅耳。

translations.literal: He did not think to build factions and strengthen neighbors, repay enmity and wipe away shame, but instead nursed resentment against the Rouran and betrayed the virtue owed Yao Xing—a petty upstart with no great strategy, fit only for brutality, and in the end he will be destroyed by others.
translations.idiomatic: He never thought to build alliances, strengthen neighbors, or avenge his ruin. Instead he picked a feud with the Rouran and betrayed Yao Xing's kindness—a petty upstart without grand strategy, fit only for brutality, and in the end others will destroy him.

sentences.zh: 」太宗大悅，語至中夜，賜浩御縹醪酒十觚，水精戎鹽一兩。

translations.literal: " Taizong was greatly pleased; they talked until midnight and he bestowed on Hao ten goblets of imperial blue-green ale and one liang of crystal frontier salt.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted. They talked until midnight, and he gave Hao ten goblets of imperial blue-green ale and one liang of crystal frontier salt.

sentences.zh: 曰：「朕味卿言，若此鹽酒，故與卿同其旨也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I savor your words as I do this salt and wine; therefore I share their flavor with you."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I savor your words as I savor this salt and wine—so I share them with you."

sentences.zh: 三年，彗星出天津，入太微，經北斗，絡紫微，犯天棓，八十餘日，至漢而滅。

translations.literal: In the third year a comet appeared at the Celestial Ford, entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, passed the Northern Dipper, threaded the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, and violated the Celestial Club; for more than eighty days it lasted until it reached Han territory and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a comet appeared at the Celestial Ford, entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, passed the Northern Dipper, threaded the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, and struck the Celestial Club. It lingered more than eighty days before reaching Han territory and fading away.

sentences.zh: 太宗復召諸儒術士問之曰：「今天下未一，四方岳峙，災咎之應，將在何國？

translations.literal: Taizong again summoned the Confucian scholars and technicians and asked: "Today the realm is not united; the four quarters stand like mountain peaks. To which state will the response of disaster and blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again summoned the scholars and diviners and asked, "The realm is not yet united and the four quarters stand like peaks. Which state will this omen strike?

sentences.zh: 朕甚畏之，盡情以言，勿有所隱。

translations.literal: I greatly fear it—speak with full candor and hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I fear it deeply. Speak with full candor and hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 」咸共推浩令對。

translations.literal: " All together urged Hao to answer.
translations.idiomatic: " All urged Hao to answer.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「古人有言，夫災異之生，由人而起。

translations.literal: Hao said: "The ancients had a saying: the birth of disasters and anomalies arises from men.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The ancients said that disasters and portents arise from human conduct.

sentences.zh: 人無釁焉，妖不自作。

translations.literal: When men have no fault, omens do not act of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When men give no cause, omens do not arise on their own.

sentences.zh: 故人失於下，則變見於上，天事恒象，百代不易。

translations.literal: Thus when men err below, changes appear above—heaven's affairs are constant in their signs, unchanging through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: When men fail below, signs appear above. Heaven's patterns are constant and do not change across the ages.

sentences.zh: 漢書載王莽篡位之前，彗星出入，正與今同。

translations.literal: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang usurped the throne, a comet came and went—exactly the same as today.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han records that before Wang Mang seized the throne, a comet appeared just as it has now.

sentences.zh: 國家主尊臣卑，上下有序，民無異望。

translations.literal: Our state has the lord honored and ministers low, upper and lower in order, and the people without divergent hopes.
translations.idiomatic: In our state the sovereign is honored and ministers are subordinate, order runs from top to bottom, and the people harbor no rival hopes.

sentences.zh: 雖僭晉卑削，主弱臣強，累世陵遲，故桓玄逼奪，劉裕秉權。

translations.literal: But the usurping Jin is base and diminished, lord weak and ministers strong, declining through successive generations—hence Huan Xuan forced seizure and Liu Yu grasped power.
translations.idiomatic: The usurping Jin court is enfeebled: its sovereign is weak and its ministers strong, and it has declined for generations. That is why Huan Xuan seized power and Liu Yu holds the reins.

sentences.zh: 彗孛者，惡氣之所生，是為僭晉將滅，劉裕篡之之應也。

translations.literal: Comets are born of malign qi—this is the response that the usurping Jin will perish and Liu Yu will usurp it.
translations.idiomatic: Comets spring from malign forces. This omen means the usurping Jin will fall and Liu Yu will seize its place.

sentences.zh: 」諸人莫能易浩言，太宗深然之。

translations.literal: " None could alter Hao's words; Taizong deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " No one could refute Hao, and the emperor was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 五年，裕果廢其主司馬德文而自立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Yu indeed deposed his lord Sima Dewen and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Liu Yu did indeed depose his sovereign Sima Dewen and take the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 南鎮上裕改元赦書。

translations.literal: The southern garrison reported Yu's edict changing the era name and granting amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The southern frontier post reported Liu Yu's edict changing the reign title and proclaiming a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時太宗幸東南潟滷池射鳥，聞之，驛召浩，謂之曰：「往年卿言彗星之占驗矣，朕於今日始信天道。」

translations.literal: At the time Taizong was visiting the southeastern salt lagoons to shoot birds; hearing this, he summoned Hao by post relay and said: "Years ago your comet prognostication has been verified—I begin today to trust heaven's way."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then hunting birds at the southeastern salt lagoons. When he heard the news he summoned Hao by courier and said, "Years ago you read the comet aright. Only today do I truly trust heaven's way."

sentences.zh: 初，浩父疾篤，浩乃剪爪截髮，夜在庭中仰禱斗極，為父請命，求以身代，叩頭流血，歲餘不息，家人罕有知者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao's father was gravely ill, Hao cut his nails and cropped his hair, and at night in the courtyard prayed upward to the Dipper Pole, pleading life for his father and asking to substitute his own body, knocking his head until it bled—for more than a year without cease, and rarely did the household know.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Hao cut his nails and hair and night after night prayed in the courtyard to the Pole Star, begging heaven to spare his father's life and offering his own in exchange. He knocked his head until it bled, and for more than a year he did not stop—almost none in the household knew.

sentences.zh: 及父終，居喪盡禮，時人稱之。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning with full rites, and men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning with full propriety, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 襲爵白馬公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Baima.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Baima.

sentences.zh: 朝廷禮儀、優文策詔、軍國書記，盡關於浩。

translations.literal: Court ritual, gracious documents, edicts and proclamations, and military and state correspondence—all passed through Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual, gracious edicts, imperial proclamations, and military and state correspondence all passed through Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩能為雜說，不長屬文，而留心於制度、科律及經術之言。

translations.literal: Hao could compose miscellaneous discourse but was not skilled at linked prose; yet he applied his mind to institutions, statutes, and the words of classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao could discourse on many subjects but was not a master of formal prose. His true attention lay in institutions, law codes, and classical learning.

sentences.zh: 作家祭法，次序五宗，蒸嘗之禮，豐儉之節，義理可觀。

translations.literal: He composed family sacrificial regulations, ordering the five ancestral lines, the rites of seasonal offerings, and the measures of abundance and frugality—principles one may admire.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted family sacrificial regulations, ordering the five ancestral lines and setting the rites of seasonal offerings with proper measures of abundance and restraint—work whose principles still command respect.

sentences.zh: 性不好老莊之書，每讀不過數十行，輒棄之，曰：「此矯誣之說，不近人情，必非老子所作。

translations.literal: By nature he did not like the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi; whenever he read he did not pass a few dozen lines before casting them aside, saying: "These are deceptive, false doctrines, not close to human feeling—they surely were not composed by Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he disliked the Laozi and Zhuangzi. He never read more than a few dozen lines before setting them aside, saying, "These are deceptive doctrines, alien to human feeling—they cannot be Laozi's own work.

sentences.zh: 老聃習禮，仲尼所師，豈設敗法文書，以亂先王之教。

translations.literal: Old Dan studied ritual—he was Confucius's teacher—how could he set up writings to ruin the law and disorder the teaching of the former kings?
translations.idiomatic: Old Dan studied ritual and was Confucius's teacher. How could he have written texts to ruin the law and overturn the teaching of the former kings?

sentences.zh: 袁生所謂家人筐篋中物，不可揚於王庭也。」

translations.literal: What Master Yuan called objects from the family basket and box—things not to be displayed in the royal court."
translations.idiomatic: They are what Master Yuan called household clutter from the basket and box—things one does not display in the royal court."

sentences.zh: 太宗恒有微疾，怪異屢見，乃使中貴人密問於浩曰：「春秋：星孛北斗，七國之君皆將有咎。

translations.literal: Taizong constantly had slight illness and strange signs appeared repeatedly; he sent a palace eunuch to question Hao in secret: "The Spring and Autumn Annals: when a comet was in the Northern Dipper, the lords of the seven states all were to have blame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often suffered minor illness, and strange omens appeared again and again. He sent a palace eunuch to question Hao in secret: "The Spring and Autumn Annals record that when a comet stood in the Northern Dipper, the lords of the seven states all faced disaster.

sentences.zh: 今茲日蝕於胃昂，盡光趙代之分野，朕疾彌年，療治無損，恐一旦奄忽，諸子並少，將如之何？

translations.literal: Now this solar eclipse is in the Stomach and Mane, its light fully in the territorial division of Zhao and Dai; my illness has lasted years and treatment brings no improvement—I fear sudden collapse; my sons are all young—what then shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: Now the sun is eclipsed in the Stomach and Mane, fully darkening the astral territory of Zhao and Dai. My illness has lasted years without improvement. I fear I may die suddenly, and my sons are all young. What then shall we do?

sentences.zh: 其為我設圖後之計。

translations.literal: Draw up for me a plan for what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: Lay out a plan for what comes after.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「陛下春秋富盛，聖業方融，德以除災，幸就平愈。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Your Majesty's years are rich and abundant, your sagely work is just merging—by virtue you may dispel disaster; may you fortunately reach full recovery.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "Your Majesty is in the prime of life and your sage virtue is still unfolding. Virtue can dispel disaster, and you will surely recover.

sentences.zh: 且天道懸遠，或消或應。

translations.literal: Moreover heaven's way is remote and suspended—it may dissolve or it may respond.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is remote and may either fade or manifest.

sentences.zh: 昔宋景見災修德，熒惑退舍。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Jing of Song saw disaster and cultivated virtue, and Mars withdrew from its lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Jing of Song saw portents and cultivated virtue, Mars withdrew from its station.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遣諸憂虞，恬神保和，納御嘉福，無以闇昧之說，致損聖思。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would dismiss all worries, calm the spirit and preserve harmony, receive auspicious blessing—do not let obscure doctrines damage your sagely thought.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to cast off worry, calm your spirit, preserve harmony, and receive heaven's blessing. Do not let dark and obscure talk harm your peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，請陳瞽言。

translations.literal: If it must be, I beg to offer blind words.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist, I will offer my blind counsel.

sentences.zh: 自聖化龍興，不崇儲貳，是以永興之始，社禝幾危。

translations.literal: Since the sage transforming influence rose like a dragon, the heir apparent was not honored—hence at the beginning of Yongxing the altars of state nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty arose, the heir apparent has not been properly established. That is why at the start of Yongxing the altars of state nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 今宜早建東宮，選公卿忠賢陛下素所委仗者使為師傅，左右信臣簡在聖心者以充賓友，入總萬機，出統戎政，監國撫軍，六柄在手。

translations.literal: Now we ought early to establish the Eastern Palace, select among the nobles and ministers those loyal and worthy whom Your Majesty has long entrusted as tutors, and trusted ministers close to the sacred heart as companions—entering to oversee the myriad affairs, going forth to command military government, overseeing the state and comforting the armies, the six handles in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should establish the Eastern Palace early. Choose loyal ministers you have long trusted as tutors, and close advisers you favor as companions. Let the heir oversee all affairs within, command the armies without, supervise the state and comfort the forces—let him hold all six powers of rule.

sentences.zh: 若此，則陛下可以優遊無為，頤神養壽，進御醫藥。

translations.literal: If so, Your Majesty may roam at ease in non-action, nourish the spirit and extend life, and advance to taking medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty may rest at ease, nourish your spirit, prolong your life, and attend to your health.

sentences.zh: 萬歲之後，國有成主，民有所歸，則姦宄息望，旁無覬覦。

translations.literal: After ten thousand years, the state will have a settled lord and the people a place to turn—then traitors will cease their hopes and none beside will covet.
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty's passing, the state will have a settled ruler and the people a place to turn. Traitors will abandon their hopes and none will dare covet the throne.

sentences.zh: 此乃萬世之令典，塞禍之大備也。

translations.literal: This is the excellent statute for ten thousand generations, the great provision for blocking calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This is the enduring statute of statecraft and the greatest safeguard against disaster.

sentences.zh: 今長皇子燾，年漸一周，明叡溫和，眾情所繫，時登儲副，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Now the eldest imperial son Tao is approaching one year, bright, wise, gentle and mild, bound to the people's feelings—if he is timely made heir, the realm will be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest prince Tao is nearly one year old—bright, wise, gentle, and beloved by all. If he is made heir now, the realm will be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 立子以長，禮之大經。

translations.literal: Establishing the son by seniority is the great constant of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the eldest son is the great constant of ritual.

sentences.zh: 若須並待成人而擇，倒錯天倫，則生履霜堅冰之禍。

translations.literal: If one must wait until all are grown to choose, reversing heaven's kinship, then arises the calamity of treading frost and solid ice.
translations.idiomatic: If you wait until all are grown before choosing, you overturn the natural order of succession and invite the disaster of treading frost until it becomes solid ice.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，載籍所記，興衰存亡，尠不由此。

translations.literal: From antiquity until now, what the records note of rise, fall, survival and perishing—few do not stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, few rises and falls recorded in the histories do not spring from this cause.

sentences.zh: 」太宗納之。

translations.literal: " Taizong accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 於是使浩奉策告宗廟，命世祖為國副主，居正殿臨朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Hao present the writ and announce it at the ancestral temple, appointing Shizu as deputy lord of the state to dwell in the main hall and hold court.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Hao present the edict at the ancestral temple and appointed Shizu deputy ruler of the state to hold court in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫嵩、山陽公奚斤、北新公安同為左輔，坐東廂西面；

translations.literal: Minister of Education Changgunsong, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin, and Duke of Beixin An Tong served as left assistants, seated in the east wing facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education Changgunsong, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin, and Duke of Beixin An Tong served as left assistants, seated in the east wing facing west;

sentences.zh: 浩與太尉穆觀、散騎常侍丘堆為右弼，坐西廂東面。

translations.literal: Hao with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Qiu Dui served as right assistants, seated in the west wing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, Grand Commandant Mu Guan, and Regular Attendant Qiu Dui served as right assistants, seated in the west wing facing east.

sentences.zh: 百僚總己以聽焉。

translations.literal: The hundred officials gathered their persons to listen.
translations.idiomatic: All officials gathered to hear their judgments.

sentences.zh: 太宗避居西宮，時隱而窺之，聽其決斷，大悅，謂左右侍臣曰：「長孫嵩宿德舊臣，歷事四世，功存社禝；

translations.literal: Taizong withdrew to the Western Palace, sometimes hiding to peer at them, listening to their decisions—greatly pleased, he told the attendants left and right: "Changgunsong is a minister of long-standing virtue, serving through four reigns, his merit preserved in the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew to the Western Palace and sometimes watched in secret, listening to their decisions. He was delighted and told his attendants, "Changgunsong is a minister of long-standing virtue who served four reigns and preserved the altars of state;

sentences.zh: 奚斤辯捷智謀，名聞遐邇；

translations.literal: Xi Jin is eloquent, quick and resourceful in stratagem, his name heard far and near;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin is eloquent and resourceful, known far and wide;

sentences.zh: 安同曉解俗情，明練於事；

translations.literal: An Tong understands popular feeling and is clear and practiced in affairs;
translations.idiomatic: An Tong understands the people's hearts and is skilled in affairs;

sentences.zh: 穆觀達於政要，識吾旨趣；

translations.literal: Mu Guan penetrates the essentials of government and knows my intent;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Guan grasps the essentials of government and knows my mind;

sentences.zh: 崔浩博聞強識，精於天人之會；

translations.literal: Cui Hao is broadly learned with powerful memory, skilled in the juncture of Heaven and man;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao is broadly learned with a powerful memory, skilled in the meeting of Heaven and human affairs;

sentences.zh: 丘堆雖無大用，然在公專謹。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui though without great use is yet in public office wholly diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui, though not greatly gifted, is wholly diligent in public duty.

sentences.zh: 以此六人輔相，吾與汝曹遊行四境，伐叛柔服，可得志於天下矣。

translations.literal: With these six men assisting, I with you all may roam the four borders, punish rebels and soften those who submit, and realize our will over the realm."
translations.idiomatic: With these six to assist him, I with you may tour the four borders, punish rebels and win over the submissive, and fulfill our will over the realm."

sentences.zh: 」羣臣時奏所疑，太宗曰：「此非我所知，當決之汝曹國主也。」

translations.literal: " When the ministers at times presented doubts, Taizong said: "This is not for me to know—you should decide it with your lord of state."
translations.idiomatic: " When ministers brought doubtful matters, the emperor said, "That is not for me to decide—you must settle it with your lord of state."

sentences.zh: 會聞劉裕死，太宗欲取洛陽、虎牢、滑臺。

translations.literal: It happened that news came of Liu Yu's death; Taizong wished to take Luoyang, Hulao, and Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Liu Yu had died, the emperor wished to seize Luoyang, Hulao, and Huatai.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「陛下不以劉裕歘起，納其使貢，裕亦敬事陛下。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Your Majesty did not disdain Liu Yu's sudden rise, received his envoys and tribute, and Yu also respected and served Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Your Majesty did not disdain Liu Yu when he rose suddenly. You received his envoys and tribute, and Liu Yu in turn honored Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 不幸今死，乘喪伐之，雖得之不令。

translations.literal: Now he has unhappily died—if we exploit his mourning to attack, though we gain it, it is not proper.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has died, to attack while they mourn may bring gain, but it is not honorable.

sentences.zh: 春秋：晉士丐帥師侵齊，聞齊侯卒，乃還。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: Jin's Shi Gai led troops to invade Qi; hearing the Marquis of Qi had died, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that when Jin's Shi Gai led troops against Qi and heard the marquis had died, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 君子大其不伐喪，以為恩足以感孝子，義足以動諸侯。

translations.literal: The noble man magnifies his not attacking during mourning, holding that grace suffices to move filial sons and righteousness suffices to stir the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The noble man praised him for not attacking during mourning, holding that such grace can move filial sons and such righteousness can stir the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 今國家亦未能一舉而定江南，宜遣人弔祭，存其孤弱，恤其凶災，布義風於天下，令德之事也。

translations.literal: Now our state also cannot in one stroke settle Jiangnan—we ought to send men to mourn and sacrifice, preserve their orphans and weak, pity their disasters, spread righteous influence through the realm: a matter of excellent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Our state cannot conquer Jiangnan in a single stroke. We should send envoys to mourn and sacrifice, protect their orphans and the weak, relieve their calamity, and spread righteous influence through the realm. That would be a deed of true virtue.

sentences.zh: 若此，則化被荊揚，南金象齒羽毛之珍，可不求而自至。

translations.literal: If so, transforming influence will cover Jing and Yang; southern gold, ivory, feathers and other treasures may come without seeking.
translations.idiomatic: Then our transforming influence will reach Jing and Yang, and southern gold, ivory, feathers, and other treasures will come without our seeking them.

sentences.zh: 裕新死，黨與未離，兵臨其境，必相率拒戰，功不可必，不如緩之，待其惡稔。

translations.literal: Yu has newly died; his faction has not dispersed—if troops press their borders they will surely join to resist; success is not certain. Better to ease off and wait until their evil ripens.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu has only just died and his faction has not yet split. If our armies press their borders they will unite to resist, and victory is not assured. Better to wait until their troubles ripen.

sentences.zh: 如其強臣爭權，變難必起，然後命將揚威，可不勞士卒，而收淮北之地。

translations.literal: If their powerful ministers contend for power, change and disaster will surely arise—then order generals to display might and, without troubling the soldiers, you may take the lands north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When their powerful ministers fight for power, turmoil will surely arise. Then send generals to show our might and take the lands north of the Huai without exhausting our troops.

sentences.zh: 」太宗銳意南伐，詰浩曰：「劉裕因姚興死而滅其國，裕死我伐之，何為不可？

translations.literal: " Taizong was keen on southern campaign and pressed Hao: "Liu Yu because Yao Xing died destroyed his state—when Yu dies I attack him; why may it not be done?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was set on a southern campaign and challenged Hao: "Liu Yu destroyed Qin when Yao Xing died. When Liu Yu dies, why may I not attack?

sentences.zh: 」浩固執曰：「興死，二子交爭，裕乃伐之。

translations.literal: " Hao stubbornly said: "When Xing died, the two sons fought each other—only then did Yu attack.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao held firm: "When Yao Xing died, his two sons fought each other. Only then did Liu Yu attack.

sentences.zh: 」太宗大怒，不從浩言，遂遣奚斤南伐。

translations.literal: " Taizong was greatly angry, did not follow Hao's words, and thereupon sent Xi Jin south to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious, rejected Hao's advice, and sent Xi Jin south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 議於監國之前曰：「先攻城也？

translations.literal: They deliberated before the overseer of the state: "Attack cities first?
translations.idiomatic: They debated before the regent: "Should we attack cities first?

sentences.zh: 先略地也？

translations.literal: Seize territory first?
translations.idiomatic: Or seize territory first?

sentences.zh: 」斤曰：「請先攻城。

translations.literal: " Jin said: "I beg to attack cities first.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi Jin said, "I urge that we attack cities first.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「南人長於守城，苻氏攻襄陽，經年不拔。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "The southerners excel at defending cities; the Fu clan attacked Xiangyang and for years could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "The southerners excel at defense. The Former Qin besieged Xiangyang for a year without success.

sentences.zh: 今以大國之力攻其小城，若不時克，挫損軍勢，敵得徐嚴而來。

translations.literal: Now with a great state's strength attacking their small cities—if we do not take them in time, we blunt our army's momentum and the enemy may leisurely strengthen and come.
translations.idiomatic: If we use a great state's strength against their small cities and fail to take them quickly, we blunt our momentum while the enemy gathers strength at leisure.

sentences.zh: 我怠彼銳，危道也。

translations.literal: We slack while they are sharp—a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: We grow weary while they grow bold—that is a perilous course.

sentences.zh: 不如分軍略地，至淮為限，列置守宰，收歛租穀。

translations.literal: Better to divide the army and seize territory, taking the Huai as limit, stationing guards and administrators, and collecting rent grain.
translations.idiomatic: Better to divide the army and seize territory up to the Huai, post governors and collectors, and gather grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 滑臺、虎牢反在軍北，絕望南救，必沿河東走。

translations.literal: Huatai and Hulao lie instead north of the army—they can despair of southern rescue and must flee east along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huatai and Hulao lie north of our army. Cut off from southern relief, the enemy must flee east along the river.

sentences.zh: 若或不然，即是囿中之物。

translations.literal: If it is not so, they are still creatures within the park enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: If not, they are still beasts within our enclosure.

sentences.zh: 」公孫表請先圖其城。

translations.literal: " Gongsun Biao asked to plan their cities first.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Biao urged that they take the cities first.

sentences.zh: 斤等濟河，先攻滑臺，經時不拔，表請濟師。

translations.literal: Jin and the others crossed the river and first attacked Huatai; after a long time could not take it, and Biao requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin crossed the river and attacked Huatai first. After a long siege failed, Gongsun Biao requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，乃親南巡。

translations.literal: Taizong was angry and personally toured south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and marched south in person.

sentences.zh: 拜浩相州刺史，加左光祿大夫，隨軍為謀主。

translations.literal: Hao was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou, promoted to Left Household Grandee, and followed the army as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou and promoted to Left Household Grandee, accompanying the army as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 及車駕之還也，浩從太宗幸西河、太原。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Hao followed Taizong in visiting Xihe and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, Hao accompanied the emperor to Xihe and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 登憇高陵之上，下臨河流，傍覽川域，慨然有感，遂與同僚論五等郡縣之是非，考秦始皇、漢武帝之違失。

translations.literal: Ascending to rest on the high mound, looking down on the river's flow and surveying the river lands at the side, he was moved with feeling and thereupon with colleagues discussed the rights and wrongs of five-rank feudalism versus commanderies and counties, examining the errors of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Resting on a high mound, he looked down on the river and surveyed the land, stirred by the sight. With his colleagues he debated the merits of feudal enfeoffment versus commanderies and counties, and examined the failures of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 好古識治，時伏其言。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity and understood governance; men of the time submitted to his words.
translations.idiomatic: He loved antiquity and understood governance, and contemporaries bowed to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 天師寇謙之每與浩言，聞其論古治亂之迹，常自夜達旦，竦意斂容，無有懈倦。

translations.literal: The Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi whenever he spoke with Hao, hearing him discourse on the traces of ancient order and chaos, often from night until dawn sat upright with composed countenance, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi spoke with Hao and heard him trace the patterns of order and chaos in antiquity, he would listen from night until dawn, sitting upright without the least sign of weariness.

sentences.zh: 既而歎美之曰：「斯言也惠，皆可底行，亦當今之皐繇也。

translations.literal: Then he sighed in admiration and said: "These words are beneficent—all may be brought to practice; he is also today's Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sighed in admiration and said, "These words are beneficent and can all be put into practice. He is the Gao Yao of our age.

sentences.zh: 但世人貴遠賤近，不能深察之耳。

translations.literal: Only the world honors what is distant and cheapens what is near—they cannot examine him deeply."
translations.idiomatic: But the world honors what is distant and cheapens what is near, and so cannot see him clearly."

sentences.zh: 」因謂浩曰：「吾行道隱居，不營世務，忽受神中之訣，當兼修儒教，輔助泰平真君，繼千載之絕統。

translations.literal: " He then said to Hao: "I practiced the Way in seclusion and did not manage worldly affairs, when suddenly I received a divine command from within— I ought jointly to cultivate Confucian teaching, assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, and continue the severed lineage of a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: " He then said to Hao, "I practiced the Way in seclusion and did not meddle in worldly affairs, when suddenly I received a divine command that I must cultivate Confucian teaching as well, assist the Perfect Lord of Great Peace, and renew a lineage severed for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 而學不稽古，臨事闇昧。

translations.literal: Yet my learning does not investigate antiquity, and facing affairs I am dim and obscure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my learning does not reach back to antiquity, and in affairs I am still blind.

sentences.zh: 卿為吾撰列王者治典，并論其大要。

translations.literal: You, for me, compile and set forth the governing canons of kings, and also discuss their great essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Compile for me the governing canons of kings, and outline their main principles.

sentences.zh: 」浩乃著書二十餘篇，上推太初，下盡秦漢變弊之迹，大旨先以復五等為本。

translations.literal: " Hao then composed more than twenty chapters, reaching upward to the Grand Beginning and tracing downward through every sign of change and decay in Qin and Han; the great thrust took restoring the five ranks as its foundation first.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then wrote more than twenty chapters, reaching back to the Grand Beginning and tracing down through the changes and decay of Qin and Han. His central aim was to restore the five ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，左右忌浩正直，共排毀之。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, those about him envied Hao's uprightness and together slandered and ruined him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, courtiers around him resented Hao's integrity and joined in slandering him.

sentences.zh: 世祖雖知其能，不免羣議，故出浩，以公歸第。

translations.literal: Though Shizu knew his ability, he could not escape the multitude of counsel, so he dismissed Hao and sent the duke home to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shizu knew his worth, he could not withstand the clamor of opinion and dismissed Hao, sending the duke home to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 及有疑議，召而問焉。

translations.literal: When there were doubtful questions in counsel, he would summon him and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a disputed question arose, Shizu would summon him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩纖妍潔白，如美婦人。

translations.literal: Hao was delicately fair, clean and white, like a beautiful woman.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was delicately fair and pale, comely as a beautiful woman.

sentences.zh: 而性敏達，長於謀計。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was quick and penetrating, excelling in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quick-witted by nature and excelled at strategy.

sentences.zh: 常自比張良，謂己稽古過之。

translations.literal: He often compared himself to Zhang Liang, saying that in investigating antiquity he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He often likened himself to Zhang Liang, claiming that his mastery of antiquity exceeded the master's own.

sentences.zh: 既得歸第，因欲修服食養性之術，而寇謙之有神中錄圖新經，浩因師之。

translations.literal: Once he had returned to his residence, he wished to cultivate the arts of ingesting elixirs and nourishing the nature; Kou Qianzhi had the Divine Central Record Chart New Classic, and Hao therefore took him as master.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he wished to practice elixir arts for cultivating life. Kou Qianzhi possessed the New Classic of the Divine Central Record Chart, and Hao became his disciple.

sentences.zh: 始光中，進爵東郡公，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era he was advanced to Duke of Dongjun and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shiguang era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongjun and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時議討赫連昌，羣臣皆以為難，唯浩曰：「往年以來，熒惑再守羽林，皆成鈎己，其占秦亡。

translations.literal: At the time they debated attacking Helian Chang; the ministers all thought it difficult, but Hao alone said: "In years past Mars has twice lodged in the Yu Lin constellation, each time forming the Gou Ji pattern—its omen is the fall of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated attacking Helian Chang, every minister deemed it too difficult—only Hao said, "For years Mars has twice held station in Yu Lin, forming the Gou Ji pattern each time. The omen reads: the fall of Qin.

sentences.zh: 又今年五星併出東方，利以西伐。

translations.literal: Moreover this year the five planets all appeared together in the east—favorable for campaigning westward.
translations.idiomatic: This year the five planets have all emerged together in the east—a sign favorable to a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 天應人和，時會並集，不可失也。

translations.literal: Heaven responds and men accord; the season and opportunity converge together—this must not be missed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men are in accord, the moment has converged—it must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 」世祖乃使奚斤等擊蒲坂，而親率輕騎襲其都城，大獲而還。

translations.literal: " Shizu then sent Xi Jin and others to strike Puban, while he personally led light cavalry to raid their capital, gaining greatly and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu sent Xi Jin and others against Puban while he personally led light cavalry in a raid on their capital. They won a great victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 及世祖復討昌，次其城下，收眾偽退。

translations.literal: When Shizu again campaigned against Chang, he halted below his city, drew up the host, and feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu renewed the campaign against Chang, he drew up beneath the city walls, then feigned a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 昌鼓譟而前，舒陣為兩翼。

translations.literal: Chang beat drums and clamored as he advanced, extending his formation into two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Chang advanced with drums beating and ranks clamoring, deploying his formation in two wings.

sentences.zh: 會有風雨從東南來，揚沙昏冥。

translations.literal: Just then wind and rain came from the southeast, raising sand into dim obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: Just then wind and rain blew in from the southeast, whipping up sand until the field went dark.

sentences.zh: 宦者趙倪進曰：「今風雨從賊後來，我向彼背，天不助人。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said: "Now wind and rain come from behind the enemy; we face them with our backs turned—Heaven does not aid men.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhao Ni stepped forward and said, "The wind and rain are coming from behind the enemy—we face them with our backs turned. Heaven is not helping us.

sentences.zh: 又將士飢渴，願陛下攝騎避之，更待後日。

translations.literal: Moreover the officers and soldiers are hungry and thirsty; I wish Your Majesty would gather the cavalry and avoid battle, waiting again for another day.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are hungry and thirsty. I beg Your Majesty to pull the cavalry back and wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 」浩叱之曰：「是何言歟！

translations.literal: " Hao rebuked him, saying: "What words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Hao snapped at him: "What sort of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 千里制勝，一日之中豈得變易？

translations.literal: To win at a thousand li—how can one alter plans within a single day?
translations.idiomatic: We laid our plan to win a thousand li away—how can we change course in a single day?

sentences.zh: 賊前行不止，後已離絕，宜分軍隱出，奄擊不意。

translations.literal: The enemy advances without cease while their rear is already cut off; we ought to divide the army, emerge hidden, and suddenly strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy presses forward without stopping while their rear is already cut off. Split the army, emerge in concealment, and strike where they do not expect it.

sentences.zh: 風道在人，豈有常也！

translations.literal: The direction of the wind lies with men—how can there be constancy in it!
translations.idiomatic: The wind is ours to command—what constancy can it have!

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰「善」。

translations.literal: " Shizu said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 分騎奮擊，昌軍大潰。

translations.literal: They divided the cavalry and struck with fierce effort; Chang's army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry split off and charged; Chang's army broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖詔尚書郎鄧淵著國記十餘卷，編年次事，體例未成。

translations.literal: At the start, Taizu ordered Secretariat Gentleman Deng Yuan to compose the National Record in more than ten rolls, arranging events by year; the form and example were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taizu had ordered Secretariat Gentleman Deng Yuan to compile the National Record in more than ten chapters, arranging events by year—but the format was never finished.

sentences.zh: 逮于太宗，廢而不述。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Taizong, it was abandoned and no longer continued.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Taizong's time the project had been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年，詔集諸文人撰錄國書，浩及弟覽、高讜、鄧穎、晁繼、范亨、黃輔等共參著作，敍成國書三十卷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui an edict gathered various literati to compile the National History; Hao, his younger brother Lan, Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Heng, Huang Fu, and others jointly participated in the composition, and completed the National History in thirty rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenrui an edict summoned scholars to compile the National History. Hao, his brother Lan, Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Heng, Huang Fu, and others joined the project and produced a thirty-chapter National History.

sentences.zh: 是年，議擊蠕蠕，朝臣內外盡不欲行，保太后固止世祖，世祖皆不聽，唯浩讚成策略。

translations.literal: That year they debated attacking the Rouran; court ministers within and without all wished not to go; the Guardian Empress Dowager firmly stopped Shizu, but Shizu would not listen to any of them—only Hao approved and completed the strategy.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court debated attacking the Rouran. Ministers inside and outside the palace opposed the campaign, and the Guardian Empress Dowager firmly urged Shizu to desist—but he listened to none of them. Only Hao endorsed the plan and saw the strategy through.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉潔、左僕射安原等乃使黃門侍郎仇齊推赫連昌太史張淵、徐辯說世祖曰：「今年己巳，三陰之歲，歲星襲月，太白在西方，不可舉兵。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director Anyuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi recommend Helian Chang's Grand Astrologer Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian to persuade Shizu, saying: "This year is jisi, a thrice-yin year; Jupiter assaults the moon, and Venus is in the west—arms must not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director Anyuan, and others had Yellow Gate Attendant Qiu Qi bring forward Helian Chang's grand astrologers Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian to persuade Shizu: "This is the jisi year, a thrice-yin year. Jupiter is assaulting the moon and Venus stands in the west. You must not mobilize the army.

sentences.zh: 北伐必敗，雖克，不利於上。

translations.literal: A northern campaign is sure to fail; even if victorious, it will not favor the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: A northern campaign is doomed to fail—and even if you win, it will bode ill for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」又羣臣共贊和淵等，云淵少時嘗諫苻堅不可南征，堅不從而敗。

translations.literal: " The ministers also together endorsed and agreed with Zhang Yuan and the rest, saying Zhang Yuan in his youth had once counseled Fu Jian that he must not campaign south; Fu Jian did not follow and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers chimed in with Zhang Yuan, noting that in his youth he had warned Fu Jian against a southern campaign—Fu Jian ignored him and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 今天時人事都不和協，何可舉動！

translations.literal: Now celestial timing and human affairs are all out of harmony—how can one mobilize!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men are out of accord—how can we march to war!

sentences.zh: 世祖意不決，乃召浩令與淵等辯之。

translations.literal: Shizu's mind was undecided, so he summoned Hao and ordered him to debate with Zhang Yuan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu could not make up his mind and summoned Hao to debate Zhang Yuan and the others.

sentences.zh: 浩難淵曰：「陽者，德也；

translations.literal: Hao countered Zhang Yuan, saying: "Yang is virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Hao challenged Zhang Yuan: "Yang is virtue;

sentences.zh: 陰者，刑也。

translations.literal: yin is punishment.
translations.idiomatic: yin is punishment.

sentences.zh: 故日蝕修德，月蝕修刑。

translations.literal: Thus at a solar eclipse one cultivates virtue; at a lunar eclipse one cultivates punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At a solar eclipse one cultivates virtue; at a lunar eclipse one cultivates punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫王者之用刑，大則陳諸原野，小則肆之市朝。

translations.literal: When kings employ punishment, on a great scale they display it in the open field; on a small scale they execute it in market and court.
translations.idiomatic: When kings wield punishment, they display it on a great scale in the open field and on a small scale in market and court.

sentences.zh: 戰伐者，用刑之大者也。

translations.literal: Warfare is the greatest application of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare is the greatest form of punishment.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，三陰用兵，蓋得其類，修刑之義也。

translations.literal: Spoken from this perspective, to use the army in a thrice-yin year accords with its kind—it is the meaning of cultivating punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, to take up arms in a thrice-yin year fits the pattern—it is the very meaning of cultivating punishment.

sentences.zh: 歲星襲月，年飢民流，應在他國，遠期十二年。

translations.literal: Jupiter assaulting the moon—famine in the year and drifting people—corresponds to another state, distant by twelve years.
