translations.idiomatic: Jupiter assaulting the moon portends famine and wandering people—but that omen applies to another state, twelve years hence.

sentences.zh: 太白行倉龍宿，於天文為東，不妨北伐。

translations.literal: Venus traversing the Azure Dragon lodge—in astronomy this is the east; it does not hinder a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Venus is passing through the Azure Dragon constellation, which in astronomy is the east—it does not obstruct a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 淵等俗生，志意淺近，牽於小數，不達大體，難與遠圖。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuan and the like are vulgar scholars, shallow in intent, tethered to petty reckonings, unable to grasp the larger design—hard to plan far with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan and his kind are shallow pedants, fixated on petty calculations and blind to the larger design—they are no partners in far-reaching plans.

sentences.zh: 臣觀天文，比年以來，月行奄昴，至今猶然。

translations.literal: Your servant observes the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered Mao, and so it remains to this day.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has covered Mao, and it still does.

sentences.zh: 其占：『三年，天子大破旄頭之國。

translations.literal: Its omen reads: "In three years the Son of Heaven will smash the state of the Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reads: "In three years the Son of Heaven will smash the state of Maotou.

sentences.zh: 』蠕蠕、高車，旄頭之眾也。

translations.literal: " The Rouran and Gaoche are the peoples of Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran and Gaoche are the peoples of Maotou.

sentences.zh: 夫聖明御時，能行非常之事。

translations.literal: When the sage and enlightened reign, they can perform extraordinary deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage sovereign holds the age, he can perform extraordinary deeds.

sentences.zh: 古人語曰：『非常之原，黎民懼焉，及其成功，天下晏然。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "At the origin of the extraordinary, the common people fear; when it succeeds, the realm is tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "At the outset of the extraordinary the people fear; when it succeeds the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 』願陛下勿疑也。

translations.literal: " I beg Your Majesty not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to hesitate.

sentences.zh: 」淵等慚而言曰：「蠕蠕，荒外無用之物，得其地不可耕而食，得其民不可臣而使，輕疾無常，難得而制，有何汲汲而苦勞士馬也？

translations.literal: " Zhang Yuan and the others, ashamed, spoke, saying: "The Rouran are a useless thing beyond the wilds; gain their land and it cannot be tilled for food, gain their people and they cannot be made subjects and employed—they are light, swift, and inconstant, hard to control—why be so urgent and toil horses and men?
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Zhang Yuan and the others replied: "The Rouran are useless barbarians beyond the frontier. Their land cannot be farmed for food; their people cannot be ruled as subjects. They are swift and unpredictable, impossible to control—why exhaust our troops and horses in such haste?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「淵言天時，是其所職，若論形勢，非彼所知。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Zhang Yuan speaks of celestial timing—that is his office; if one discusses strategic situation, that is not what they know.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Zhang Yuan speaks of celestial timing—that is his profession. But if we discuss strategic realities, that lies beyond his competence.

sentences.zh: 斯乃漢世舊說常談，施之於今，不合事宜也。

translations.literal: This is old Han-dynasty common talk; applied to the present it does not suit present circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: That is stale Han-dynasty common talk—applied today it no longer fits the facts.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why do I say so?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 夫蠕蠕者，舊是國家北邊叛隸，今誅其元惡，收其善民，令復舊役，非無用也。

translations.literal: The Rouran were once rebel vassals on our state's northern border; now execute their chief villains, gather their good people, and make them resume old service—they are not useless.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were once rebel subjects on our northern frontier. Execute their ringleaders, take their good people, and restore them to their old duties—they are far from useless.

sentences.zh: 漠北高涼，不生蚊蚋，水草美善，夏則北遷。

translations.literal: North of the desert it is high and cool; mosquitoes and gnats do not breed there; grass and water are fine and good; in summer they migrate north.
translations.idiomatic: North of the desert the land is high and cool, free of mosquitoes and gnats, with fine grass and water—they migrate there each summer.

sentences.zh: 田牧其地，非不可耕而食也。

translations.literal: To farm and herd that land—it is not impossible to cultivate and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Farm and herd that land—it can certainly be cultivated for food.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕子弟來降，貴者尚公主，賤者將軍、大夫，居滿朝列，又高車號為名騎，非不可臣而畜也。

translations.literal: Rouran youths who came to surrender—the noble married princesses, the lowly became generals and grandees, filling the court ranks; moreover the Gaoche are famed as elite cavalry—it is not impossible to subject and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran who have surrendered marry princesses at the top and fill the ranks of generals and grandees below; the Gaoche are famed as elite cavalry—they can be ruled and kept.

sentences.zh: 夫以南人追之，則患其輕疾，於國兵則不然。

translations.literal: For southerners pursuing them, they would fear their lightness and speed; with our state's army it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners who pursue them fear their speed—but our state's army is another matter.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 彼能遠走，我亦能遠逐，與之進退，非難制也。

translations.literal: They can run far; we too can pursue far; matching them in advance and retreat—it is not hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: They can flee far—we can pursue far. Matching them move for move, they are not hard to control.

sentences.zh: 且蠕蠕往數入國，民吏震驚。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rouran have repeatedly entered the realm; officials and people are shaken in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Rouran have raided our borders again and again, leaving officials and common people in terror.

sentences.zh: 今夏不乘虛掩進，破滅其國，至秋復來，不得安臥。

translations.literal: If this summer we do not exploit their emptiness and strike secretly to destroy their state, when autumn comes they will return again and we cannot rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not strike now while they are exposed and destroy their state this summer, they will return in autumn and we will never sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 自太宗之世，迄於今日，無歲不驚，豈不汲汲乎哉！

translations.literal: From Emperor Taizong's age down to today, not a year without alarm—is this not urgent!
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Taizong's reign to this day, not a year has passed without alarm—is the need not urgent!

sentences.zh: 世人皆謂淵、辯通解數術，明決成敗。

translations.literal: The world all says Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian thoroughly understand numerology and clearly decide success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone says Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian master numerology and can read success and failure with clarity.

sentences.zh: 臣請試之，問其西國未滅之前有何亡徵。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to test them—inquire what signs of doom there were before the western state fell.
translations.idiomatic: Let me put them to the test: ask what omens foretold the fall of the western state before it was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 知而不言，是其不忠；

translations.literal: If they knew and did not speak, that is their disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: If they knew and said nothing, that is disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 若實不知，是其無術。

translations.literal: if they truly did not know, that is their lack of art.
translations.idiomatic: if they truly did not know, that is incompetence.

sentences.zh: 」時赫連昌在座，淵等自以無先言，慚赧而不能對。

translations.literal: " At the time Helian Chang was present; Zhang Yuan and the others, thinking they had given no prior warning, flushed with shame and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang was present. Zhang Yuan and the others, ashamed that they had foretold nothing, flushed and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悅，謂公卿曰：「吾意決矣。

translations.literal: Shizu was greatly pleased and told the ministers: "My mind is decided.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was delighted and told the ministers: "My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 亡國之師不可與謀，信矣哉。

translations.literal: Counsellors of a fallen state cannot be consulted in planning—true indeed!
translations.idiomatic: One cannot take counsel from the advisers of a fallen state—how true that is!

sentences.zh: 」而保太后猶難之，復令羣臣於保太后前評議。

translations.literal: " Yet the Guardian Empress Dowager still objected and again ordered the ministers to debate and assess before her.
translations.idiomatic: But the Guardian Empress Dowager still objected and ordered the ministers to debate the matter again in her presence.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂浩曰：「此等意猶不伏，卿善曉之令悟。」

translations.literal: Shizu told Hao: "These people's minds still are not convinced—you must speak well and make them understand."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu told Hao: "These people still are not persuaded. Speak to them clearly and make them see reason."

sentences.zh: 既罷朝，或有尤浩者曰：「今吳賊南寇而舍之北伐。

translations.literal: After court was dismissed, someone blamed Hao, saying: "Now the Wu rebels raid from the south, yet you abandon them to campaign north.
translations.idiomatic: After court adjourned, someone reproached Hao: "The Wu rebels are raiding from the south, yet you would leave them and march north.

sentences.zh: 行師千里，其誰不知。

translations.literal: An army marches a thousand li—who does not know?
translations.idiomatic: An army marching a thousand li—who will not know?

sentences.zh: 若蠕蠕遠遁，前無所獲，後有南賊之患，危之道也。

translations.literal: If the Rouran flee far, with nothing gained ahead and southern rebel trouble behind—that is the path of peril.
translations.idiomatic: If the Rouran flee beyond reach, we gain nothing in front while southern rebels threaten us from behind—that is the road to disaster.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 今年不摧蠕蠕，則無以禦南賊。

translations.literal: If we do not crush the Rouran this year, we cannot defend against the southern rebels.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not crush the Rouran this year, we cannot defend against the southern rebels.

sentences.zh: 自國家并西國以來，南人恐懼，揚聲動眾以衞淮北。

translations.literal: Since the state annexed the western realm, the southerners have been in fear, raising armies and moving hosts to guard north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Since our state annexed the western realm, the southerners have lived in fear, mustering armies to defend the north bank of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 彼北我南，彼勞我息，其勢然矣。

translations.literal: They north, we south; they labor, we rest—such is the momentum.
translations.idiomatic: They march north while we march south; they toil while we rest—such is the balance of forces.

sentences.zh: 比破蠕蠕，往還之間，故不見其至也。

translations.literal: By the time we crush the Rouran and go there and back, therefore we will not see them arrive.
translations.idiomatic: By the time we defeat the Rouran and return, they will not have arrived.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why do I say so?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 劉裕得關中，留其愛子，精兵數萬，良將勁卒，猶不能固守，舉軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Liu Yu gained Guanzhong, left his beloved son there with tens of thousands of elite troops, excellent generals and crack soldiers—yet still could not hold firm, and the entire army was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu took Guanzhong and left his beloved son there with tens of thousands of crack troops and fine generals—yet they could not hold it, and the whole army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 號哭之聲，至今未已。

translations.literal: The sound of wailing has not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The wailing has not stopped to this day.

sentences.zh: 如何正當國家休明之世，士馬強盛之時，而欲以駒犢齒虎口也？

translations.literal: How, just when the state is in a flourishing and bright age and troops and horses are strong, would you set foals and calves against a tiger's jaws?
translations.idiomatic: Why, at the height of our state's glory, when our armies and horses are at their strongest, would you set foals and calves against a tiger's maw?

sentences.zh: 設令國家與之河南，彼必不能守之。

translations.literal: Even if the state gave them Henan, they would surely be unable to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we gave them Henan, they could not hold it.

sentences.zh: 自量不能守，是以必不來。

translations.literal: Measuring themselves unable to hold it, therefore they surely will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they cannot hold it, they will surely not come.

sentences.zh: 若或有眾，備邊之軍耳。

translations.literal: If they have any host at all, it will be border-guard troops only.
translations.idiomatic: If they do send forces, it will be border-guard troops and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 夫見瓶水之凍，知天下之寒；

translations.literal: See ice on a bottle of water, and know the cold of the world;
translations.idiomatic: See ice on a bottle of water and you know the cold of the world;

sentences.zh: 嘗肉一臠，識鑊中之味。

translations.literal: taste one slice of meat, and know the flavor in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: taste one slice of meat and you know the flavor in the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 物有其類，可推而得也。

translations.literal: Things have their kind—one can infer and obtain the conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Things belong to kinds—you can infer the whole from a part.

sentences.zh: 且蠕蠕恃其絕遠，謂國家力不能至，自寬來久，故夏則散眾放畜，秋肥乃聚，背寒向溫，南來寇抄。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rouran rely on their extreme distance, thinking the state's strength cannot reach them; relaxed for a long time, therefore in summer they disperse the host and release herds; when autumn fatness comes they gather; turning from cold toward warmth, they come south to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran trust in their remoteness and believe our state cannot reach them. Complacent for years, they disperse their herds each summer and gather only when the animals grow fat in autumn—then they turn from the cold toward warmth and raid south.

sentences.zh: 今出其慮表，攻其不備。

translations.literal: Now strike beyond their expectations and attack where they are unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Strike beyond their expectations and attack where they are unprepared.

sentences.zh: 大軍卒至，必驚駭星分，望塵奔走。

translations.literal: When the great army arrives suddenly, they will be startled and scatter like stars, fleeing at the sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: When our main force arrives suddenly, they will scatter in terror and flee at the first sight of our dust.

sentences.zh: 牡馬護群，牝馬戀駒，驅馳難制，不得水草，未過數日則聚而困敝，可一舉而滅。

translations.literal: Stallions guard the herd, mares cling to foals; driven hard they are hard to control; without grass and water, within a few days they gather exhausted—we can destroy them in one blow.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions guard the herd while mares cling to their foals—driven hard they are impossible to control. Deprived of grass and water, within days they will cluster in exhaustion and we can destroy them at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 暫勞永逸，長久之利，時不可失也。

translations.literal: Brief toil for lasting ease, a long-term benefit—the time cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: A brief effort for lasting peace—a permanent gain. The moment must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 唯患上無此意，今聖慮已決，發曠世之謀，如何止之？

translations.literal: I only feared the sovereign lacked this intent; now sagely deliberation is decided and a plan of the ages is launched—how can it be stopped?
translations.idiomatic: I only feared Your Majesty lacked this resolve—but now the sage decision is made and a plan for the ages is set in motion. How can it be stopped?

sentences.zh: 陋矣哉，公卿也！

translations.literal: How shallow, the ministers!
translations.idiomatic: How narrow-minded the ministers are!

sentences.zh: 」諸軍遂行。

translations.literal: " The armies then marched.
translations.idiomatic: The armies marched.

sentences.zh: 天師謂浩曰：「是行也，如之何，果可克乎？

translations.literal: The Celestial Master said to Hao: "This expedition—how will it go; can victory truly be won?
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Master asked Hao: "This campaign—how do you think it will go? Can we truly win?

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「天時形勢，必克無疑。

translations.literal: " Hao replied: "Celestial timing and strategic situation—victory is certain without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Hao answered: "By celestial timing and strategic advantage, victory is certain beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 但恐諸將瑣瑣，前後顧慮，不能乘勝深入，使不全舉耳。」

translations.literal: Only I fear the generals will be petty and trivial, looking forward and backward with concern, unable to follow victory with a deep thrust, so that the expedition may not be fully accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: My only fear is that the generals will prove petty and timid, hesitating at every turn and unable to pursue the victory in depth, so that we fail to finish the job completely."

sentences.zh: 及軍入其境，蠕蠕先不設備，民畜布野，驚怖四奔，莫相收攝。

translations.literal: When the army entered their territory, the Rouran at first made no preparations; people and livestock lay scattered across the wilds, fleeing in terror in all directions with none gathering or restraining them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army entered Rouran territory, the enemy at first made no preparations. People and livestock lay scattered across the countryside, fleeing in terror in all directions with no one to rally or restrain them.

sentences.zh: 於是分軍搜討，東西五千里，南北三千里，凡所俘虜及獲畜產車廬，彌漫山澤，蓋數百萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army was divided to search and round up; east and west five thousand li, north and south three thousand li—all captives taken and livestock, carts and tents seized filled mountains and marshes, numbering several millions.
translations.idiomatic: The army was then divided to search and round up the land—five thousand li east to west, three thousand li north to south. Captives taken and livestock, carts, and tents seized filled the mountains and marshes, numbering in the millions.

sentences.zh: 高車殺蠕蠕種類，歸降者三十餘萬落。

translations.literal: The Gaoche killed Rouran of their kind; those who submitted numbered more than thirty myriad households.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche slaughtered Rouran tribesmen, and more than three hundred thousand households came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 虜遂散亂矣。

translations.literal: The barbarians were thus scattered and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was thus scattered and broken.

sentences.zh: 世祖沿弱水西行，至涿邪山，諸大將果疑深入有伏兵，勸世祖停止不追。

translations.literal: Shizu marched west along the Ruoshui River to Zhuoxie Mountain; the great generals indeed suspected that pushing deep might mean ambush, and urged Shizu to halt and not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marched west along the Ruoshui River to Zhuoxie Mountain. The senior generals indeed feared that a deep advance might lead into ambush and urged Shizu to halt and abandon the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 天師以浩曩日之言，固勸世祖窮討，不聽。

translations.literal: The Celestial Master, relying on Hao's words of the other day, firmly urged Shizu to pursue to the end; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Master, citing Hao's earlier prediction, firmly urged Shizu to pursue the enemy to the end, but Shizu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後有降人，言蠕蠕大檀先被疾，不知所為，乃焚燒穹廬，科車自載，將數百人入山南走。

translations.literal: Later a surrendered man said that Datan of the Rouran had first fallen ill, not knowing what to do; he then burned his yurts, loaded carts himself, and with several hundred men fled south into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Later a defector reported that Datan of the Rouran had fallen ill first and, not knowing what to do, burned his yurts, loaded carts himself, and fled south into the mountains with several hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 民畜窘聚，方六十里中，無人領統。

translations.literal: People and livestock were pressed together in distress; within an area of sixty li square, none were in command.
translations.idiomatic: People and livestock were pressed together in panic across an area sixty li square, with no one left in command.

sentences.zh: 相去百八十里，追軍不至，乃徐徐西遁，[1]唯此得免。

translations.literal: At a distance of one hundred eighty li, the pursuit army did not arrive; they then slowly fled westward,[1] only thus did they escape.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred eighty li away, the pursuit army never arrived, and they slowly fled westward[1]—only thus did they escape.

sentences.zh: 後聞涼州賈胡言，若復前行二日，則盡滅之矣。

translations.literal: Later it was heard from Liangzhou merchant-barbarians that if the army had advanced another two days, they would have been entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was reported by merchant-traders from Liangzhou that if the army had pushed on for two more days, the Rouran would have been utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 世祖深恨之。

translations.literal: Shizu deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu deeply regretted the missed opportunity.

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，南賊竟不能動，如浩所量。

translations.literal: Once the great army had returned, the southern enemy indeed could not stir—just as Hao had estimated.
translations.idiomatic: Once the main army had returned, the southern enemy could not stir after all—just as Hao had predicted.

sentences.zh: 浩明識天文，好觀星變。

translations.literal: Hao had clear knowledge of astronomy and loved to observe changes in the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had a keen understanding of astronomy and loved to watch for changes among the stars.

sentences.zh: 常置金銀銅鋌於酢器中，令青，夜有所見即以鋌畫紙作字以記其異。

translations.literal: He often placed gold, silver, and copper ingots in vinegar vessels to turn them green; whenever he observed something at night, he would at once use an ingot to inscribe characters on paper to record the anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: He often placed gold, silver, and copper ingots in vinegar to turn them green, and whenever he observed something at night he would immediately use an ingot to inscribe characters on paper and record the portent.

sentences.zh: 世祖每幸浩第，多問以異事。

translations.literal: Whenever Shizu visited Hao's residence, he often questioned him about strange matters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shizu visited Hao's home, he often questioned him about strange and uncanny matters.

sentences.zh: 或倉卒不及束帶，奉進蔬食，不暇精美。

translations.literal: Sometimes in haste he had no time to gird his sash, and would serve plain food without leisure for refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes in haste he had no time even to gird his sash and would serve plain food with no chance to make it fine.

sentences.zh: 世祖為舉匕箸，或立嘗而旋。

translations.literal: Shizu would lift the spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand to taste and then return.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu would lift the spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand to taste the food and then withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其見寵愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor and affection shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor and affection he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 於是引浩出入臥內，加侍中、特進、撫軍大將軍、左光祿大夫，賞謀謨之功。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hao was admitted in and out of the inner quarters; he was further given Palace Attendant, Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Honorary Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, rewarding his merit in counsel and planning.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was then admitted in and out of the inner quarters and further promoted to Palace Attendant, Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Honorary Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, in reward for his counsel and planning.

sentences.zh: 世祖從容渭浩曰：「卿才智淵博，事朕祖考，忠著三世，朕故延卿自近。

translations.literal: Shizu said at ease to Hao: "Your talent and learning are profound and broad; you served my ancestors and grandfather, loyalty renowned through three generations—I therefore keep you close.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said calmly to Hao: "Your talent and learning are profound and broad. You served my ancestors and grandfather, and your loyalty has shone through three generations. That is why I keep you close at hand.

sentences.zh: 其思盡規諫，匡予弼予，勿有隱懷。

translations.literal: Consider how to exhaust yourself in remonstrance and counsel; correct me and assist me, and harbor no hidden reservations.
translations.idiomatic: Think always how to remonstrate and counsel to the full; correct me and assist me, and keep nothing hidden in your heart.

sentences.zh: 朕雖當時遷怒，若或不用，久久可不深思卿言也。

translations.literal: Although I may at the moment shift my anger, if I do not use your counsel at once, in time how could I fail to deeply ponder your words?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I turn my anger on you in the moment and do not heed you at once, in time how could I fail to weigh your words deeply?

sentences.zh: 」因令歌工歷頌群臣，事在長孫道生傳。

translations.literal: " He then ordered singers to recite in turn the praises of the ministers—the matter is in the biography of Changsun Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered singers to recite in turn the praises of his ministers—the account is given in the biography of Changsun Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 又召新降高車渠帥數百人，賜酒食於前。

translations.literal: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and feasted them with wine and food before him.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and feasted them with wine and food in his presence.

sentences.zh: 世祖指浩以示之，曰：「汝曹視此人，尫纖懦弱，手不能彎弓持矛，其胸中所懷，乃踰於甲兵。

translations.literal: Shizu pointed to Hao to show them, saying: "You look at this man—slender, frail, and weak; his hands cannot bend a bow or wield a spear, yet what he holds within his breast surpasses armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu pointed to Hao and showed him to them, saying: "Look at this man—slender, frail, and weak; his hands cannot bend a bow or wield a spear, yet what he carries in his breast surpasses armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 朕始時雖有征討之意，而慮不自決，前後克捷，皆此人導吾令至此也。

translations.literal: At first I had the intention to campaign, yet I worried I could not decide for myself; the successive victories before and after—all were because this man guided me to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: At first I had the will to campaign but feared I could not decide for myself. The victories won before and since have all come because this man guided me to where I stand today.

sentences.zh: 」乃敕諸尚書曰：「凡軍國大計，卿等所不能決，皆先諮浩，然後施行。」

translations.literal: " He then charged the Ministers of the Secretariat: "For all great plans of army and state that you cannot decide, consult Hao first, then carry them out."
translations.idiomatic: " He then charged the Ministers of the Secretariat: "For every major plan of army and state that you cannot decide, consult Hao first, then carry it out."

sentences.zh: 俄而南藩諸將表劉義隆大嚴，欲犯河南。

translations.literal: Before long the generals of the southern frontier memorialized that Liu Yilong was making great military preparations and intended to invade Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the generals of the southern frontier reported that Liu Yilong was making great military preparations and intended to invade Henan.

sentences.zh: 請兵三萬，先其未發逆擊之，因誅河北流民在界上者，絕其鄉導，足以挫其銳氣，使不敢深入。

translations.literal: They requested thirty thousand troops to strike back before the enemy could launch, and by executing the northern stream refugees at the border, cut off their guides—enough to blunt their keen edge and keep them from advancing deep.
translations.idiomatic: They requested thirty thousand troops to strike before the enemy could launch, execute the northern refugees at the border, cut off their guides, blunt their fighting spirit, and keep them from advancing deep.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿議之，咸言宜許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to discuss it; all said it should be approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministers to discuss the proposal, and all said it should be approved.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「此不可從也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This must not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "This must not be followed.

sentences.zh: 往年國家大破蠕蠕，馬力有餘，南賊震懼，常恐輕兵奄至，臥不安席，故先聲動眾，以備不虞，非敢先發。

translations.literal: In past years the state utterly defeated the Rouran; our horses still have strength to spare. The southern enemy is shaken with fear, constantly dreading that light troops will suddenly arrive—they cannot sleep in peace. Therefore they raise alarms and move forces first, to guard against the unexpected; they do not dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: In past years the state utterly defeated the Rouran, and our horses still have strength to spare. The southern enemy is shaken with fear, constantly dreading that light troops will suddenly arrive—they cannot sleep in peace. They raise alarms and move troops first to guard against the unexpected; they do not dare strike first.

sentences.zh: 又南土下濕，夏月蒸暑，水潦方多，草木深邃，疾疫必起，非行師之時。

translations.literal: Moreover the southern lands are low and damp; in summer's months steaming heat prevails, floods are abundant, grass and trees grow deep and dense, and pestilence is sure to arise—it is no season for marching armies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the southern lands are low and damp. In summer the heat is stifling, floods are abundant, and grass and trees grow thick and deep—pestilence is sure to arise. This is no season for marching armies.

sentences.zh: 且彼先嚴有備，必堅城固守。

translations.literal: Moreover they will have taken precautions first and prepared defenses; they will surely hold their fortified cities fast.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they will have taken precautions first and prepared their defenses; they will surely hold their fortified cities fast.

sentences.zh: 屯軍攻之，則糧食不給；

translations.literal: If we encamp troops to besiege them, provisions will not suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If we encamp troops to besiege them, provisions will not suffice;

sentences.zh: 分兵肆討，則無以應敵。

translations.literal: if we divide the army to raid widely, we will have no means to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: if we divide the army to raid widely, we will have no means to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 未見其利。

translations.literal: I see no advantage in it.
translations.idiomatic: I see no advantage in it.

sentences.zh: 就使能來，待其勞倦，秋涼馬肥，因敵取食，徐往擊之，萬全之計，勝必可克。

translations.literal: Even if they can come, wait until they are weary; when autumn is cool and horses are fat, take food from the enemy, advance slowly to strike them—a plan of complete security, victory is surely attainable.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they do come, wait until they are weary. When autumn turns cool and horses grow fat, take food from the enemy and advance slowly to strike them—that is a plan of complete security, and victory is surely attainable.

sentences.zh: 在朝群臣及西北守將，從陛下征討，西滅赫連，北破蠕蠕，多獲美女珍寶，馬畜成群。

translations.literal: The ministers at court and the frontier generals of the northwest who followed Your Majesty in campaigns west destroyed Helian, north broke the Rouran, and gained many beautiful women, treasures and jewels, horses and livestock in herds.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers at court and the frontier generals of the northwest who followed Your Majesty in campaigns destroyed Helian in the west and broke the Rouran in the north, gaining many beautiful women, treasures and jewels, and horses and livestock in herds.

sentences.zh: 南鎮諸將聞而生羨，亦欲南抄，以取資財。

translations.literal: The generals of the southern commanderies heard and grew envious; they too wish to raid south to seize goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The generals of the southern commanderies heard of this and grew envious; they too wished to raid south and seize goods and wealth.

sentences.zh: 是以披毛求瑕，妄張賊勢，冀得肆心。

translations.literal: Therefore they pick at hairs to find flaws, falsely inflate the enemy's strength, hoping to indulge their own desires.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they pick at hairs to find flaws, falsely inflate the enemy's strength, and hope to indulge their own desires.

sentences.zh: 既不獲聽，故數稱賊動，以恐朝廷。

translations.literal: Since they did not obtain approval, they repeatedly report enemy movements to frighten the court.
translations.idiomatic: Since they did not obtain approval, they repeatedly report enemy movements to frighten the court.

sentences.zh: 背公存私，為國生事，非忠臣也。

translations.literal: They betray the public for private gain and stir trouble for the state—they are no loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They betray the public for private gain and stir trouble for the state—they are no loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 」世祖從浩議。

translations.literal: " Shizu followed Hao's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu followed Hao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 南鎮諸將復表賊至，而自陳兵少，簡幽州以南戍兵佐守，就漳水造船，嚴以為備。

translations.literal: The southern commandery generals again memorialized that the enemy had arrived, but themselves declared their troops too few; they requested selecting garrison soldiers south of Youzhou to assist in defense, building ships on the Zhang River, and tightening preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The southern commandery generals again reported that the enemy had arrived, but themselves declared their troops too few. They requested selecting garrison soldiers south of Youzhou to assist in defense, building ships on the Zhang River, and tightening preparations.

sentences.zh: 公卿議者僉然，欲遣騎五千，并假署司馬楚之、魯軌、韓延之等，令誘引邊民。

translations.literal: Those discussing among the ministers were unanimous, wishing to dispatch five thousand cavalry and concurrently provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to lure border peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Those discussing among the ministers were unanimous, wishing to dispatch five thousand cavalry and concurrently provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to lure border peoples over.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「非上策也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This is not the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "This is not the superior stratagem.

sentences.zh: 彼聞幽州已南精兵悉發，大造舟船，輕騎在後，欲存立司馬，誅除劉族，必舉國駭擾，懼於滅亡，當悉發精銳，來備北境。

translations.literal: When they hear that elite troops south of Youzhou have all been dispatched and ships are being built in great number, with light cavalry in the rear intending to establish Sima and exterminate the Liu clan, the whole state will be shaken with alarm, fearing destruction; they will surely dispatch all elite forces to guard the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear that elite troops south of Youzhou have all been dispatched, that ships are being built in great number, and that light cavalry in the rear intend to establish Sima and exterminate the Liu clan, the whole state will be shaken with alarm and fear destruction. They will surely dispatch all elite forces to guard the northern border.

sentences.zh: 後審知官軍有聲無實，恃其先聚，必喜而前行，徑來至河，肆其侵暴，則我守將無以禦之。

translations.literal: Later when they ascertain that our official army has sound but no substance, relying on their prior massing they will surely rejoice and advance, coming straight to the river and unleashing their ravages—then our frontier generals will have no means to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they ascertain that our official army has sound but no substance, relying on their prior massing they will surely rejoice and advance, coming straight to the river and unleashing their ravages—then our frontier generals will have no means to resist.

sentences.zh: 若彼有見機之人，善設權譎，乘間深入，虞我國虛，生變不難，非制敵之良計。

translations.literal: If they have men who see opportunities, skilled in deceit and ruse, who exploit a gap to push deep, anticipating our state's emptiness—stirring rebellion would not be hard; this is no good plan for controlling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If they have men who see opportunities, skilled in deceit and ruse, who exploit a gap to push deep and anticipate our state's weakness, stirring rebellion would not be hard. This is no good plan for controlling the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今公卿欲以威力攘賊，乃所以招令速至也。

translations.literal: Now the ministers wish to drive off the enemy with show of force—this is precisely what will summon and hurry their arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ministers wish to drive off the enemy with a show of force—this is precisely what will summon and hurry their arrival.

sentences.zh: 夫張虛聲而召實害，此之謂矣。

translations.literal: To raise empty clamor and summon real harm—this is the saying.
translations.idiomatic: To raise empty clamor and summon real harm—this is the very thing.

sentences.zh: 不可不思，後悔無及。

translations.literal: It must be pondered; regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: This must be pondered; regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 我使在彼，期四月前還。

translations.literal: Our envoys are there; they are expected to return before the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Our envoys are there and are expected to return before the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 可待使至，審而後發，猶未晚也。

translations.literal: We can wait until the envoys arrive, verify, then act—it will still not be late.
translations.idiomatic: We can wait until the envoys arrive, verify the situation, and then act—it will still not be too late.

sentences.zh: 且楚之之徒，是彼所忌，將奪其國，彼安得端坐視之。

translations.literal: Moreover men like Chuzhi are what they dread, for they will seize their state—how could they sit at ease and watch?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover men like Chuzhi are what they dread, for they will seize their state—how could they sit at ease and watch?

sentences.zh: 故楚之往則彼來，止則彼息，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Thus when Chuzhi goes, they come; when he stops, they quiet—such is the tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Chuzhi goes, they come; when he stops, they quiet—such is the tendency.

sentences.zh: 且楚之等瑣才，能招合輕薄無賴，而不能成就大功。

translations.literal: Moreover Chuzhi and his kind are petty talents—able to gather the frivolous and the rogue, but unable to accomplish great deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Chuzhi and his kind are petty talents—able to gather the frivolous and the rogue, but unable to accomplish great deeds.

sentences.zh: 為國生事，使兵連禍結，必此之群矣。

translations.literal: Stirring trouble for the state and linking war with disaster—it will surely be this crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Stirring trouble for the state and linking war with disaster—it will surely be this crowd.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗聞魯軌說姚興求入荊州，至則散敗，乃不免蠻賊掠賣為奴，使禍及姚泓，已然之效。

translations.literal: Your subject once heard that Lu Gui persuaded Yao Xing to enter Jingzhou; when he arrived he scattered and was defeated, and could not escape being captured and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, bringing calamity upon Yao Hong—a lesson already proven.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once heard that Lu Gui persuaded Yao Xing to enter Jingzhou; when he arrived his forces scattered and were defeated, and he could not escape being captured and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, bringing calamity upon Yao Hong—a lesson already proven.

sentences.zh: 」浩復陳天時不利於彼，曰：「今茲害氣在揚州，不宜先舉兵，一也；

translations.literal: " Hao again set forth that celestial timing was unfavorable for them, saying: "This year injurious qi is in Yangzhou—it is unsuitable to raise troops first—first point;
translations.idiomatic: " Hao again set forth that celestial timing was unfavorable for them, saying: "This year injurious qi is in Yangzhou—it is unsuitable to raise troops first—first point;

sentences.zh: 午歲自刑，先發者傷，二也；

translations.literal: the year of wu bears self-punishment—he who strikes first will be harmed—second point;
translations.idiomatic: the year of wu bears self-punishment—he who strikes first will be harmed—second point;

sentences.zh: 日蝕滅光，晝昏星見，飛鳥墮落，宿值斗牛，憂在危亡，三也；

translations.literal: a solar eclipse extinguishing light, stars appearing in daytime dimness, birds falling from the sky, the lodge positioned at Niu and Dou—woe lies in peril and destruction—third point;
translations.idiomatic: a solar eclipse extinguishing light, stars appearing in daytime dimness, birds falling from the sky, the lodge positioned at Niu and Dou—woe lies in peril and destruction—third point;

sentences.zh: 熒惑伏匿於翼軫，戒亂及喪，四也；

translations.literal: Mars hiding in Yi and Zhen, warning of disorder and mourning—fourth point;
translations.idiomatic: Mars hiding in Yi and Zhen, warning of disorder and mourning—fourth point;

sentences.zh: 太白未出，進兵者敗，五也。

translations.literal: Venus has not yet risen; he who advances troops will be defeated—fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: Venus has not yet risen; he who advances troops will be defeated—fifth point.

sentences.zh: 夫興國之君，先修人事，次盡地利，後觀天時，故萬舉而萬全，國安而身盛。

translations.literal: Now a king who raises a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts the advantages of terrain, and afterward observes celestial timing—thus ten thousand undertakings and ten thousand successes, state secure and person flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: A king who raises a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts the advantages of terrain, and afterward observes celestial timing—thus ten thousand undertakings and ten thousand successes, state secure and person flourishing.

sentences.zh: 今義隆新國，是人事未周也；

translations.literal: Today Yilong's state is new—this means human affairs are not yet complete;
translations.idiomatic: Today Yilong's state is new—this means human affairs are not yet complete;

sentences.zh: 災變屢見，是天時不協也；

translations.literal: disasters and portents appear repeatedly—this means celestial timing is not in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: disasters and portents appear repeatedly—this means celestial timing is not in harmony;

sentences.zh: 舟行水涸，是地利不盡也。

translations.literal: boats sail but the waters are dry—this means terrain's advantages are not fully realized.
translations.idiomatic: boats sail but the waters are dry—this means the advantages of terrain are not fully realized.

sentences.zh: 三事無一成，自守猶或不安，何得先發而攻人哉？

translations.literal: None of the three matters is fulfilled; even in self-defense one might not be secure—how could one strike first and attack others?
translations.idiomatic: None of the three matters is fulfilled; even in self-defense one might not be secure—how could one strike first and attack others?

sentences.zh: 彼必聽我虛聲而嚴，我亦承彼嚴而動，兩推其咎，皆自以為應敵。

translations.literal: They will surely hear our empty clamor and tighten defenses; we too will respond to their tightening and move—each side pushing blame, each believing itself responding to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely hear our empty clamor and tighten defenses; we too will respond to their tightening and move—each side pushing blame, each believing itself responding to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兵法當分災迎受害氣，未可舉動也。」

translations.literal: By military art one should divide disaster and ward off injurious qi—it is not yet time to act."
translations.idiomatic: By military art one should divide disaster and ward off injurious qi—it is not yet time to act."

sentences.zh: 世祖不能違眾，乃從公卿議。

translations.literal: Shizu could not go against the multitude and followed the ministers' counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu could not go against the multitude and followed the ministers' counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩復固爭，不從。

translations.literal: Hao again argued stubbornly; his counsel was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao argued stubbornly again, but his counsel was not followed.

sentences.zh: 遂遣陽平王杜超鎮鄴，琅邪王司馬楚之等屯潁川。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, was sent to guard Ye; the Prince of Langye, Sima Chuzhi, and others encamped at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Prince of Yangping, Du Chao, was sent to guard Ye, and the Prince of Langye, Sima Chuzhi, and others encamped at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 於是賊來遂疾，到彥之自清水入河，泝流西行，分兵列守南岸，西至潼關。

translations.literal: Then the enemy came swiftly indeed; Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui, sailed upstream west, divided troops to line and guard the south bank, westward to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Then the enemy came swiftly indeed. Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui, sailed upstream west, divided his troops to line and guard the south bank, and advanced westward to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞赫連定與劉義隆懸分河北，乃治兵，欲先討赫連。

translations.literal: Shizu heard that Helian Ding and Liu Yilong had made a distant agreement to partition Hebei; he marshalled troops, intending first to attack Helian.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard that Helian Ding and Liu Yilong had made a distant agreement to partition Hebei. He marshalled troops, intending first to attack Helian.

sentences.zh: 群臣曰：「義隆猶在河中，舍之西行，前寇未可必克，而義隆乘虛，則失東州矣。

translations.literal: The ministers said: "Yilong is still in the river region; if we leave him and march west, the enemy before us cannot be surely conquered, and if Yilong seizes the vacuum, we will lose the eastern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said: "Yilong is still in the river region. If we leave him and march west, the enemy before us cannot be surely conquered, and if Yilong seizes the opportunity, we will lose the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 」世祖疑焉，問計於浩。

translations.literal: " Shizu was doubtful and asked Hao for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu was doubtful and asked Hao for counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「義隆與赫連定同惡相招，連結馮跋，牽引蠕蠕，規肆逆心，虛相唱和。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Yilong and Helian Ding invite each other as fellow evildoers, link with Feng Ba, draw in the Rouran, scheme rebellious hearts, and hollowly echo each other.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Yilong and Helian Ding invite each other as fellow evildoers, link with Feng Ba, draw in the Rouran, scheme rebellious hearts, and hollowly echo each other.

sentences.zh: 義隆望定進，定待義隆前，皆莫敢先入。

translations.literal: Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong to go first—neither dares enter first.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong to go first—neither dares enter first.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，有似連雞，不得俱飛，無能為害也。

translations.literal: In your subject's view it is like tethered chickens—they cannot fly together and can do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: In your subject's view it is like tethered chickens—they cannot fly together and can do no harm.

sentences.zh: 臣始謂義隆軍來當屯住河中，兩道北上，東道向冀州，西道衝鄴。

translations.literal: Your subject originally thought when Yilong's army came it would encamp in the river region and march north on two routes—eastern toward Jizhou, western striking Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject originally thought that when Yilong's army came it would encamp in the river region and march north on two routes—eastern toward Jizhou, western striking Ye.

sentences.zh: 如此，則陛下當自致討，不得徐行。

translations.literal: If so, Your Majesty would need to take the field yourself and could not advance leisurely.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Your Majesty would need to take the field yourself and could not advance leisurely.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，東西列兵，徑二千里，一處不過數千，形分勢弱。

translations.literal: Now it is not so—they line troops east and west for two thousand li straight, nowhere more than several thousand; form divided, strength weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so. They line troops east and west for two thousand li straight, nowhere more than several thousand—form divided, strength weakened.

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，儜兒情見，止望固河自守，免死為幸，無北渡意也。

translations.literal: From this one sees the weakling's intent revealed—he only hopes to hold the river fast and defend himself; escaping death is his good fortune; he has no intention of crossing north.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees the weakling's intent revealed—he only hopes to hold the river fast and defend himself; escaping death is his good fortune; he has no intention of crossing north.

sentences.zh: 赫連定殘根易摧，擬之必仆。

translations.literal: Helian Ding's withered root is easily broken; push him and he will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ding's withered root is easily broken; push him and he will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 克定之後，東出潼關，席卷而前，則威震南極，江淮以北無立草矣。

translations.literal: After conquering and settling him, march east out of Tong Pass and sweep forward—then awe will shake the southern pole; north of the Yangzi and Huai no blade of grass will stand.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering and settling him, march east out of Tong Pass and sweep forward—then awe will shake the southern pole, and north of the Yangzi and Huai no blade of grass will stand.

sentences.zh: 聖策獨發，非愚近所及，願陛下西行勿疑。

translations.literal: Your sage strategy arises alone—not something the near and foolish can reach; I pray Your Majesty march west without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your sage strategy arises alone—not something the near and foolish can reach. I pray Your Majesty march west without doubt.

sentences.zh: 」平涼既平，其日宴會，世祖執浩手以示蒙遜使曰：「所云崔公，此是也。

translations.literal: " After Pingliang was pacified, that day at the banquet Shizu took Hao's hand to show Mengsun's envoy: "The Lord Cui I spoke of—this is he.
translations.idiomatic: " After Pingliang was pacified, that day at the banquet Shizu took Hao's hand to show Mengsun's envoy: "The Lord Cui I spoke of—this is he.

sentences.zh: 才略之美，當今無比。

translations.literal: The beauty of his talent and strategy—in the present age there is none to compare.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of his talent and strategy—in the present age there is none to compare.

sentences.zh: 朕行止必問，成敗決焉，若合符契，初無失矣。

translations.literal: In my comings and goings I always ask him; success and failure are decided thereby—as if tally halves matched, from the first there has been no failure.
translations.idiomatic: In my comings and goings I always ask him; success and failure are decided thereby—as if tally halves matched, from the first there has been no failure.

sentences.zh: 」後冠軍將軍安頡軍還，獻南俘，因說南賊之言云，義隆敕其諸將，若北國兵動，先其未至，徑前入河，若其不動，住彭城勿進。

translations.literal: " Later General Champion An Bi's army returned and presented southern captives; he accordingly reported the southern enemy's words—that Yilong had charged his generals: if the northern state moves troops, before they arrive go straight into the river; if they do not move, stop at Pengcheng and do not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Later General Champion An Bi's army returned and presented southern captives. He accordingly reported the southern enemy's words—that Yilong had charged his generals: if the northern state moves troops, before they arrive go straight into the river; if they do not move, stop at Pengcheng and do not advance.

sentences.zh: 如浩所量。

translations.literal: Just as Hao had estimated.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Hao had predicted.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂公卿曰：「卿輩前謂我用浩計為謬，驚怖固諫。

translations.literal: Shizu said to the ministers: "You formerly said my use of Hao's plan was wrong, and in alarm firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said to the ministers: "You formerly said my use of Hao's plan was wrong, and in alarm firmly remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 常勝之家，始皆自謂踰人遠矣，至於歸終，乃不能及。

translations.literal: In a house that always wins, at first all deem themselves far beyond others; when it comes to the final accounting, they cannot catch up.
translations.idiomatic: In a house that always wins, at first all deem themselves far beyond others; when it comes to the final accounting, they cannot catch up.

sentences.zh: 」遷浩司徒。

translations.literal: " Hao was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao was transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時方士祁纖奏立四王，以日東西南北為名，欲以致禎吉，除災異。

translations.literal: At that time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings, named for the sun's east, west, south, and north, wishing thereby to bring auspicious fortune and remove disasters and portents.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings, named for the sun's east, west, south, and north, wishing thereby to bring auspicious fortune and remove disasters and portents.

sentences.zh: 詔浩與學士議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hao and the erudites to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hao and the erudites to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「先王建國以作蕃屏，不應假名以為其福。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "When former kings established states to serve as border screens, they should not borrow names for their fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "When former kings established states to serve as border bulwarks, they did not borrow auspicious names to secure their fortune.

sentences.zh: 夫日月運轉，周歷四方，京都所居，在於其內，四王之稱，實奄邦畿，名之則逆，不可承用。

translations.literal: The sun and moon revolve, circling through the four directions; the capital where the emperor dwells lies within them. The title 'four kings' would in truth encompass the imperial domain—naming them thus would be contrary to order and cannot be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon wheel through the four quarters, and the imperial capital sits at their center. To call them 'four kings' would in truth swallow up the royal domain itself; such a name reverses proper order and cannot be accepted.

sentences.zh: 」先是，纖奏改代為萬年，浩曰：「昔太祖道武皇帝，應天受命，開拓洪業，諸所制置，無不循古。

translations.literal: " Previously, Xian had memorialized changing Dai to Wannian. Hao said: "In the past, Emperor Daowu, the Taizu Emperor, received Heaven's mandate and opened up the great enterprise; in all institutions he established, there was none that did not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, Xian had memorialized to change Dai to Wannian. Hao said, "In the past Emperor Daowu, our Taizu, received Heaven's mandate and opened the great enterprise; in every institution he established, he followed the ancient models.

sentences.zh: 以始封代土，後稱為魏，故代、魏兼用，猶彼殷商。

translations.literal: Because his first enfeoffment was on Dai soil and he later took the name Wei, both Dai and Wei are used together, like the Yin and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: His first fief lay in the land of Dai, and he later took the name Wei; thus Dai and Wei are used together, as with Yin and Shang of old.

sentences.zh: 國家積德，著在圖史，當享萬億，不待假名以為益也。

translations.literal: The state's accumulated virtue is recorded in the annals and charts—it should enjoy ten thousand ages; it does not need to borrow a name for added benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's accumulated virtue is written in the charts and annals; it is destined to endure ten thousand generations and needs no borrowed name to add to its blessing.

sentences.zh: 纖之所聞，皆非正義。

translations.literal: What Xian has heard is none of it in accord with right principle.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing Xian has heard accords with right principle.

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之。

translations.literal: " Shizu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 是時，河西王沮渠牧犍，內有貳意，世祖將討焉，先問於浩。

translations.literal: At that time, Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, harbored rebellious intentions inwardly. Shizu was about to attack him and first asked Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, harbored disloyal intentions. The Emperor was about to campaign against him and first consulted Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「牧犍惡心已露，不可不誅。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "Mujian's wicked heart has already been exposed—he cannot but be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "Mujian's wicked heart is already exposed—he must be punished.

sentences.zh: 官軍往年北伐，雖不克獲，實無所損。

translations.literal: The official army's northern campaign of previous years, though it did not capture the enemy, in truth suffered no loss.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army's northern campaign of previous years, though it took no captives, in truth suffered no real loss.

sentences.zh: 于時行者內外軍馬三十萬匹，計在道死傷不滿八千，歲常羸死，恒不減萬，乃不少於此。

translations.literal: At that time those on the march numbered three hundred thousand horses inside and outside; counting those dead and wounded on the road, they did not reach eight thousand. In ordinary years those that die from emaciation are never less than ten thousand—thus no fewer than this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the forces on the march, inside and out, numbered three hundred thousand horses; those dead and wounded on the road did not reach eight thousand. In an ordinary year, horses lost to emaciation never fall below ten thousand—so the campaign cost us no more than the usual toll.

sentences.zh: 而遠方承虛，便謂大損，不能復振。

translations.literal: Yet distant lands, receiving empty reports, then say there was great loss and that recovery is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet distant lands, hearing empty rumors, declare that we suffered crippling losses and can never recover.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，不圖大軍卒至，必驚駭騷擾，不知所出，擒之必矣。

translations.literal: Now, taking them by surprise—they will not expect the great army to arrive suddenly—they will surely be alarmed and thrown into turmoil, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Strike them now by surprise—they will never expect the great army to appear so suddenly. They will panic and scatter, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain.

sentences.zh: 且牧犍劣弱，諸弟驕恣，爭權從橫，民心離解。

translations.literal: Moreover Mujian is inferior and weak; his younger brothers are arrogant and unrestrained, contending for power in every direction, and the hearts of the people are estranged and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mujian himself is weak; his younger brothers are arrogant and unrestrained, scrambling for power in every direction, and the people's hearts are already divided.

sentences.zh: 加比年以來，天災地變，都在秦涼，成滅之國也。

translations.literal: Add to this that in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's transformations have all been in Qin and Liang—it is a state ripe for destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this that in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's portents have all fallen upon Qin and Liang—it is a kingdom ripe for destruction.

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「善，吾意亦以為然。

translations.literal: " Shizu said: "Good—I too think it so.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Good—I am of the same mind.

sentences.zh: 」命公卿議之。

translations.literal: " He ordered the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the ministers to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 弘農王奚斤等三十餘人皆曰：「牧犍西垂下國，雖心不純臣，然繼父職貢，朝廷接以蕃禮。

translations.literal: Prince of Hongnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others all said: "Mujian is a state on the western frontier; though his heart is not purely that of a subject, he has succeeded his father in tribute duties, and the court has received him with the rites due a vassal frontier state.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hongnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others all said, "Mujian is a petty state on the western frontier. Though his loyalty is not pure, he has succeeded his father in paying tribute, and the court has treated him with the rites due a frontier vassal.

sentences.zh: 又王姬釐降，罪未甚彰，謂宜羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Moreover the princess sent in marriage has just arrived; his crimes are not yet very manifest—we say restraint and conciliation are enough.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the imperial princess has only just been sent to him in marriage, and his crimes are not yet fully exposed—we hold that restraint and conciliation are enough.

sentences.zh: 今士馬勞止，宜可小息。

translations.literal: Now soldiers and horses are weary and halted—it is fit to rest a little.
translations.idiomatic: Our soldiers and horses are weary and need rest.

sentences.zh: 又其地鹵斥，略無水草，大軍既到，不得久停。

translations.literal: Moreover his territory is saline and barren, with almost no water or grass. Once the great army arrives, it cannot remain long.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his land is saline and barren, with scarcely any water or grass. Once the great army arrives, it cannot remain long.

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍來，必完聚城守，攻則難拔，野無所掠。

translations.literal: When they hear the army is coming, they will surely fortify and concentrate to hold the cities; assault will be hard to succeed, and in the countryside there will be nothing to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear the army is coming, they will surely fortify their cities and hold them. Assault will be hard to succeed, and the countryside will offer nothing to plunder.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書古弼、李順之徒皆曰：「自溫圉河以西，至於姑臧城南，[2]天梯山上冬有積雪，深一丈餘，至春夏消液，下流成川，引以溉灌。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Director of the Masters of Writing Gu Bi, Li Shun, and the like all said: "From west of the Wenji River to south of Guzang city, [2] on Tianti Mountain winter snow accumulates more than ten feet deep; by spring and summer it melts and flows downward forming streams, drawn off for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Gu Bi, Director of the Masters of Writing, Li Shun, and others all said, "From west of the Wenji River to south of Guzang city, [2] on Tianti Mountain snow accumulates in winter more than ten feet deep; by spring and summer it melts and flows down in streams that are diverted for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍至，決此渠口，水不通流，則致渴乏。

translations.literal: When they hear the army is coming, they will breach these canal mouths so water cannot flow—then thirst and want will ensue.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear the army is coming, they will breach these canal mouths and cut off the water—then thirst and want will follow.

sentences.zh: 去城百里之內，赤地無草，又不任久停軍馬。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li of the city the ground is bare red earth without grass, and again it cannot bear long encampment of army and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li of the city the ground is bare red earth without grass, and again the army and horses cannot remain there long.

sentences.zh: 斤等議是也。

translations.literal: Jin's proposal is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others are right.

sentences.zh: 」世祖乃命浩以其前言與斤共相難抑。

translations.literal: " Shizu thereupon ordered Hao to use his earlier words to debate and refute Jin jointly.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon ordered Hao to use his earlier arguments to debate and rebut Jin.

sentences.zh: 諸人不復餘言，唯曰「彼無水草」。

translations.literal: The others had no further arguments—only saying "there is no water or grass there."
translations.idiomatic: The others had no further arguments and could only repeat, "There is no water or grass there."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「漢書地理志稱：『涼州之畜，為天下饒。

translations.literal: Hao said: "The Geographic Treatise of the Book of Han states: 'The livestock of Liang Province are the richest under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The Geographic Treatise of the Book of Han states, 'The livestock of Liang Province are the richest under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 』若無水草，何以畜牧？

translations.literal: " If there were no water or grass, how could there be pasturage?
translations.idiomatic: " If there were no water or grass, how could there be pasturage?

sentences.zh: 又漢人為居，終不於無水草之地築城郭、立郡縣也。

translations.literal: Moreover Han people dwell there—they would never build city walls and establish commanderies and counties in a place without water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han people live there—they would never build walled cities and establish commanderies and counties in a place without water or grass.

sentences.zh: 又雪之消液，纔不斂塵，何得通渠引漕，溉灌數百萬頃乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the melted snow—barely enough to dampen dust—how could it form canals for irrigation and water millions of qing of fields?
translations.idiomatic: And as for melted snow—barely enough to dampen the dust—how could it fill canals and irrigate millions of qing of fields?

sentences.zh: 此言大詆誣於人矣。

translations.literal: This talk is gross slander and deception of people.
translations.idiomatic: This is gross slander, a deliberate deception.

sentences.zh: 」李順等復曰：「耳聞不如目見，吾曹目見，何可共辨！

translations.literal: " Li Shun and others again said: "What the ear hears is not equal to what the eye sees—we have seen with our own eyes; how can we debate together!"
translations.idiomatic: " Li Shun and the others replied, "What the ear hears is not equal to what the eye sees—we have seen it ourselves; there is nothing to debate!"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「汝曹受人金錢，欲為之辭，謂我目不見便可欺也！

translations.literal: " Hao said: "You have received someone's gold and wish to speak for him—you think because my eyes do not see, you can deceive me!"
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "You have taken someone's gold and wish to speak on his behalf—you think that because I have not seen it with my own eyes, you can deceive me!"

sentences.zh: 」世祖隱聽，聞之乃出，親見斤等，辭旨嚴厲，形於神色。

translations.literal: " Shizu had been listening in secret; hearing this he came forth and saw Jin and the others in person. His words were stern and severe, showing in his bearing and expression.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor had been listening in secret. Hearing this, he came forth and confronted Jin and the others in person. His words were stern and severe, and it showed in his face.

sentences.zh: 群臣乃不敢復言，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: The ministers then dared speak no more—they merely assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then dared speak no further and merely assented.

sentences.zh: 於是遂討涼州而平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Liang Province and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he campaigned against Liang Province and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 多饒水草，如浩所言。

translations.literal: It was rich in water and grass, just as Hao had said.
translations.idiomatic: The land was rich in water and grass, just as Hao had said.

sentences.zh: 乃詔浩曰：「昔皇祚之興，世隆北土，積德累仁，多歷年載，澤流蒼生，義聞四海。

translations.literal: An edict addressed Hao: "In times past the imperial fortune arose; generation after generation it flourished in the northern lands, accumulating virtue and heaping benevolence through many years. Its bounty flowed to the black-haired people; its righteousness was heard throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed Hao: "In times past the imperial fortune arose; generation after generation it flourished in the northern lands, heaping virtue and benevolence through many years. Its bounty flowed to the people; its righteousness was heard throughout the four seas.

sentences.zh: 我太祖道武皇帝，協順天人，以征不服，應期撥亂，奄有區夏。

translations.literal: Our Taizu Emperor Daowu harmonized with Heaven and man to campaign against the unsubmissive; responding to the age he swept away disorder and suddenly possessed the Central Realms.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu Emperor Daowu harmonized Heaven and man to campaign against the unsubmissive; responding to the age, he swept away disorder and suddenly possessed the Central Realms.

sentences.zh: 太宗承統，光隆前緒，釐正刑典，大業惟新。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong succeeded the line, gloriously exalting the prior undertakings, rectifying the penal code—the great enterprise renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong succeeded the line, gloriously carrying forward the prior undertakings, rectifying the penal code—the great enterprise made new.

sentences.zh: 然荒域之外，猶未賓服。

translations.literal: Yet beyond the wild domains, some still have not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond the wild domains, some still have not submitted in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 此祖宗之遺志，而貽功於後也。

translations.literal: This is the legacy purpose of the ancestors—a merit bequeathed to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: This is the legacy purpose of the ancestors—a task bequeathed to posterity.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇身，獲奉宗廟，戰戰兢兢，如臨淵海，懼不能負荷至重，繼名丕烈。

translations.literal: I, with my slight person, have obtained the charge of the ancestral temple. Fearful and cautious, as if standing by a deep abyss, I fear I cannot bear the utmost weight or continue the grand fame.
translations.idiomatic: I, with my slight person, have received charge of the ancestral temple. Fearful and trembling, as if standing beside a deep abyss, I fear I cannot bear this utmost weight or continue the grand fame.

sentences.zh: 故即位之初，不遑寧處，揚威朔裔，掃定赫連。

translations.literal: Therefore at the start of my accession, without leisure for repose, I displayed might on the northern frontier and swept away Helian.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from the first days of my accession, without leisure for repose, I displayed might on the northern frontier and swept away Helian.

sentences.zh: 逮於神䴥，始命史職注集前功，以成一代之典。

translations.literal: Reaching the Shengui era, I first ordered the historiographers to record and compile prior achievements, to complete the canon of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Shengui era, I first ordered the historiographers to record and compile prior achievements, to complete the canon of our age.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，戎旗仍舉，秦隴克定，徐兗無塵，平逋寇於龍川，討孽豎於涼域。

translations.literal: Since then the martial banners have repeatedly been raised: Qin and Long were pacified, Xu and Yan were without dust; fugitive rebels were settled at Longchuan, and wicked usurpers were punished in the Liang domain.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the martial banners have repeatedly been raised: Qin and Long were pacified, Xu and Yan cleared of dust; fugitive rebels were settled at Longchuan, and wicked usurpers were punished in the Liang domain.

sentences.zh: 豈朕一人獲濟於此，賴宗廟之靈，群公卿士宣力之効也。

translations.literal: How could I alone have succeeded herein? I rely on the spirit of the ancestral temple and the effect of all ministers and officials exerting their strength.
translations.idiomatic: How could I alone have succeeded in this? I rely on the spirit of the ancestral temple and the exertions of all my ministers and officials.

sentences.zh: 而史闕其職，篇籍不著，每懼斯事之墜焉。

translations.literal: Yet the historians neglect their duty—the records are not written. I always fear this matter will fall into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the historians neglect their duty and the records remain unwritten. I always fear this work will be lost.

sentences.zh: 公德冠朝列，言為世範，小大之任，望君存之。

translations.literal: Your virtue crowns the court ranks; your words are a model for the age. In duties great and small, I look to you to preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue crowns the court; your words are a model for the age. In duties great and small, I look to you to preserve them.

sentences.zh: 命公留臺，綜理史務，述成此書，務從實錄。

translations.literal: I appoint you to remain at the capital, oversee historiographical affairs, narrate and complete this book—see that it follows the truth of the record.
translations.idiomatic: I appoint you to remain at the capital, oversee historiographical affairs, and narrate this book to completion—see that it follows the truth of the record.

sentences.zh: 」浩於是監祕書事，以中書侍郎高允、散騎侍郎張偉參著作，續成前紀。

translations.literal: " Hao thereupon supervised Secretarial affairs; he appointed Zhongshu Attendant Gao Yun and Cavalier Attendant Zhang Wei as associate compilers and continued to complete the prior annals.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao thereupon supervised Secretarial affairs. He appointed Zhongshu Attendant Gao Yun and Cavalier Attendant Zhang Wei as associate compilers and continued to complete the prior annals.

sentences.zh: 至於損益褒貶，折中潤色，浩所總焉。

translations.literal: As for additions and deletions, praise and blame, weighing and harmonizing, and polishing—these Hao oversaw in total.
translations.idiomatic: As for additions and deletions, praise and blame, weighing and harmonizing, and polishing—these Hao oversaw entirely.

sentences.zh: 及恭宗始總百揆，浩復與宜都王穆壽輔政事。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Gongzong began to oversee all affairs of state, Hao again together with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou assisted in governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Gongzong began to oversee all affairs of state, Hao again assisted in governance together with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou.

sentences.zh: 時又將討蠕蠕，劉潔復致異議。

translations.literal: At that time they were again about to campaign against the Rouran, and Liu Jie again raised objections.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were again about to campaign against the Rouran, and Liu Jie again raised objections.

sentences.zh: 世祖逾欲討之，乃召問浩。

translations.literal: Shizu all the more wished to attack them; he summoned and questioned Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor all the more wished to attack them and summoned Hao to consult him.

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「往擊蠕蠕，師不多日，潔等各欲回還。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "On the previous attack on the Rouran, the army had not been out many days when Jie and the others each wished to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "On the previous campaign against the Rouran, the army had not been out many days when Jie and the others each wished to turn back.

sentences.zh: 後獲其生口，云軍還之時，去賊三十里。

translations.literal: Later we captured their living captives, who said that when the army returned, they were thirty li from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Later we captured their living captives, who said that when the army withdrew, they were only thirty li from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 是潔等之計過矣。

translations.literal: Thus Jie and the others' plan was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jie and the others' plan was wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫北土多積雪，至冬時常避寒南徙。

translations.literal: The northern lands accumulate much snow; by winter they usually move south to escape the cold.
translations.idiomatic: The northern lands accumulate deep snow; in winter the Rouran usually move south to escape the cold.

sentences.zh: 若因其時，潛軍而出，必與之遇，則可擒獲。

translations.literal: If we take advantage of that season and send the army out secretly, we are sure to encounter them—and then capture is possible.
translations.idiomatic: If we take advantage of that season and send the army out secretly, we are sure to encounter them—and capture will follow.

sentences.zh: 」世祖以為然。

translations.literal: " Shizu considered it correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃分軍為四道，詔諸將俱會鹿渾海。

translations.literal: He divided the army into four routes and decreed that all generals should assemble at Luhun Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the army into four columns and decreed that all generals should assemble at Luhun Lake.

sentences.zh: 期日有定，而潔恨計不用，沮誤諸將，無功而還。

translations.literal: The date was set—but Jie, resenting that his plan was not adopted, discouraged and misled the generals, and they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The rendezvous date was set, but Jie, resenting that his plan was not adopted, discouraged and misled the generals, and they returned without success.

sentences.zh: 事在潔傳。

translations.literal: The matter is in Jie's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in Jie's biography.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，詔浩與尚書、順陽公蘭延都督行臺中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shizu toured the west and decreed that Hao together with the Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Shunyang Lan Yan, should oversee the Mobile Secretariat and all military affairs inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor toured the west and decreed that Hao, together with the Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Shunyang Lan Yan, should oversee the Mobile Secretariat and all military affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 世祖至東雍，親臨汾曲，觀叛賊薛永宗壘，進軍圍之。

translations.literal: Shizu reached Eastern Yong, personally coming to Fenqu to observe the rebel Xue Yongzong's fortifications; he advanced and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reached Eastern Yong, personally coming to Fenqu to observe the rebel Xue Yongzong's fortifications, then advanced and besieged them.

sentences.zh: 永宗出兵欲戰，世祖問浩曰：「今日可擊不？

translations.literal: Yongzong sent troops out wishing to fight. Shizu asked Hao: "Can we attack today?"
translations.idiomatic: Yongzong sent troops out to give battle. The Emperor asked Hao, "Can we attack today?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「永宗未知陛下自來，人心安閑，北風迅疾，宜急擊之，須臾必碎。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Yongzong does not yet know Your Majesty has come in person—the people's hearts are calm and at ease. The north wind is swift and fierce—you should strike quickly; in a moment he will be shattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "Yongzong does not yet know Your Majesty has come in person—the people's hearts are calm and untroubled. The north wind is swift and fierce; strike quickly and he will be shattered in a moment.

sentences.zh: 若待明日，恐其見官軍盛大，必夜遁走。

translations.literal: If you wait until tomorrow, I fear when he sees the official army's great array he will flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: If you wait until tomorrow, I fear that once he sees the imperial army's great array he will flee by night.

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之。

translations.literal: " Shizu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 永宗潰滅。

translations.literal: Yongzong was routed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzong was routed and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 車駕濟河，前驅告賊在渭北。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported the rebels were north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported that the rebels were north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 世祖至洛水橋，賊已夜遁。

translations.literal: Shizu reached the Luo River bridge—the rebels had already fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reached the Luo River bridge—the rebels had already fled by night.

sentences.zh: 詔問浩曰：「蓋吳在長安北九十里。

translations.literal: An edict questioned Hao: "Gai Wu is ninety li north of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: An edict questioned Hao: "Gai Wu is ninety li north of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 渭北地空，穀草不備。

translations.literal: North of the Wei the land is empty and grain and fodder are not prepared.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Wei the land is empty and grain and fodder are not prepared.

sentences.zh: 欲渡渭南西行，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to cross south of the Wei and proceed west—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to cross south of the Wei and proceed west—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「蓋吳營去此六十里，賊魁所在。

translations.literal: " Hao replied: "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here—the rebel chief's location.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here—that is where the rebel chief is.

sentences.zh: 擊蛇之法，當須破頭，頭破則尾豈能復動。

translations.literal: The method for striking a snake: one must break the head; once the head is broken, how can the tail move again?
translations.idiomatic: The method for striking a snake is to break the head; once the head is broken, how can the tail move again?

sentences.zh: 宜乘勢先擊吳。

translations.literal: One should seize the momentum and strike Wu first.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the momentum and strike Wu first.

sentences.zh: 今軍往，一日便到。

translations.literal: If the army goes now, in one day it will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: If the army goes now, it will arrive in a single day.

sentences.zh: 平吳之後，回向長安，亦一日而至。

translations.literal: After pacifying Wu, turning back toward Chang'an is also one day's march.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Wu, turning back toward Chang'an is also a single day's march.

sentences.zh: 一日之內，未便損傷。

translations.literal: Within one day, harm will not yet be incurred.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day, no real harm will be done.

sentences.zh: [3]愚謂宜從北道。

translations.literal: [3] I foolishly consider we should take the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: [3] I humbly hold that we should take the northern route.

sentences.zh: 若從南道，則蓋吳徐入北山，卒未可平。

translations.literal: If we take the southern route, then Gai Wu will slowly enter the northern mountains—and in the end he cannot be pacified.
