translations.idiomatic: If we take the southern route, Gai Wu will slip slowly into the northern mountains—and in the end he cannot be pacified.

sentences.zh: 」世祖不從，乃渡渭南。

translations.literal: " Shizu did not follow this and crossed south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not follow this advice and crossed south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳聞世祖至，盡散入北山，果如浩言，軍無所克。

translations.literal: When Wu heard Shizu had arrived, they all dispersed into the northern mountains—exactly as Hao had said—and the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard the Emperor had arrived, they all dispersed into the northern mountains—exactly as Hao had said—and the army achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 世祖悔之。

translations.literal: Shizu regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor regretted it.

sentences.zh: 後以浩輔東宮之勤，賜繒絮布帛各千段。

translations.literal: Later, for Hao's diligence in assisting the Eastern Palace, he was granted one thousand bolts each of silk floss, cloth, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for Hao's diligence in assisting the Eastern Palace, he was granted one thousand bolts each of silk floss, cloth, and silk.

sentences.zh: 著作令史太原閔湛、趙郡郄標素諂事浩，乃請立石銘，刊載國書，并勒所注五經。

translations.literal: Compilers' clerk Min Zhan of Taiyuan and Qie Biao of Zhao Commandery had long flattered and served Hao; they thereupon requested establishing stone inscriptions to carve and publish the national history, and also to engrave the Five Classics as he had annotated them.
translations.idiomatic: Compilers' clerk Min Zhan of Taiyuan and Qie Biao of Zhao Commandery had long fawned upon Hao; they thereupon requested erecting stone inscriptions to carve and publish the national history, and also to engrave the Five Classics as he had annotated them.

sentences.zh: 浩贊成之。

translations.literal: Hao approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 恭宗善焉，遂營於天郊東三里，方百三十步，用功三百萬乃訖。

translations.literal: Gongzong considered it good; they therefore built at three li east of the Celestial Suburb, one hundred thirty paces square—a labor cost of three million before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong approved it, and they built at three li east of the Celestial Suburb, one hundred thirty paces square—a labor cost of three million before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 世祖蒐于河西，詔浩詣行在所議軍事。

translations.literal: Shizu held a hunt in Hexi and decreed Hao to come to the mobile palace to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held a hunt in Hexi and decreed that Hao come to the mobile palace to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 浩表曰：「昔漢武帝患匈奴強盛，故開涼州五郡，通西域，勸農積穀，為滅賊之資。

translations.literal: Hao submitted a memorial: "In the past Emperor Wu of Han, troubled by the Xiongnu's strength, therefore opened the five commanderies of Liang Province, connected with the Western Regions, encouraged farming and accumulated grain—as resources for destroying the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hao submitted a memorial: "In the past Emperor Wu of Han, troubled by the Xiongnu's strength, opened the five commanderies of Liang Province, connected with the Western Regions, encouraged farming and accumulated grain—as resources for destroying the enemy.

sentences.zh: 東西迭擊。

translations.literal: East and west struck in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: East and west struck in alternation.

sentences.zh: 故漢未疲，而匈奴已弊，後遂入朝。

translations.literal: Thus Han was not yet weary while the Xiongnu were already exhausted—and later they came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Han was not yet exhausted while the Xiongnu were already spent—and in the end they came to court.

sentences.zh: 昔平涼州，臣愚以為北賊未平，征役不息，可不徙其民，案前世故事，計之長者。

translations.literal: When Liang Province was pacified before, this humble servant thought the northern enemy was not yet pacified and levies and corvée did not cease—we could not relocate its people. Following the precedents of former ages, this was the far-sighted plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Province was pacified before, this humble servant held that with the northern enemy not yet pacified and levies and corvée unceasing, we should not relocate its people. Following the precedents of former ages, that was the far-sighted plan.

sentences.zh: 若遷民人，則土地空虛，雖有鎮戍，適可禦邊而已，至於大舉，軍資必乏。

translations.literal: If the people are relocated, the land will be empty and deserted; though there are garrison posts, they can only just defend the border—as for a major campaign, military supplies will surely be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are relocated, the land will lie empty; though garrison posts remain, they can only just defend the border—as for a major campaign, military supplies will surely run short.

sentences.zh: 陛下以此事闊遠，竟不施用。

translations.literal: Your Majesty considered this matter too remote and expansive—and in the end did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty considered this matter too remote and far-reaching, and in the end did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚意，猶如前議，募徙豪強大家，充實涼土，軍舉之日，東西齊勢，此計之得者。」

translations.literal: In this humble servant's view, it is still as in the earlier proposal: recruit and relocate powerful magnate families to fill and strengthen the Liang lands; when the army is raised, east and west will combine their strength—this is the plan that succeeds."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, I stand by my earlier proposal: recruit and relocate powerful magnate families to populate and strengthen the Western Regions; when the army is mobilized, east and west will combine forces—this is the plan that will succeed."

sentences.zh: 浩又上五寅元曆，表曰：「太宗即位元年，敕臣解急就章、孝經、論語、詩、尚書、春秋、禮記、周易。

translations.literal: Hao furthermore submitted the Wuyin Original Calendar, memorializing: "In the first year of Taizong's accession, Your Majesty decreed that I explain the Jijiuzhang, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Record of Rites, and Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also submitted the Wuyin Original Calendar in a memorial: "In the first year of Emperor Taizong's accession, Your Majesty commanded me to interpret the Jijiuzhang, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Record of Rites, and Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 三年成訖。

translations.literal: Three years later it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the work was complete.

sentences.zh: 復詔臣學天文、星曆、易式、九宮，無不盡看。

translations.literal: Again Your Majesty decreed I study astronomy, star calendars, the Yishi divination art, and the Nine Palaces—I examined them all without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty then commanded me to study astronomy, star calendrics, the Yishi divination methods, and the Nine Palaces art—and I read them all without exception.

sentences.zh: 至今三十九年，晝夜無廢。

translations.literal: From then until now, thirty-nine years—I have not ceased by day or night.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, thirty-nine years—I have not slackened day or night.

sentences.zh: 臣禀性弱劣，力不及健婦人，更無餘能，是以專心思書，忘寢與食，至乃夢共鬼爭義。

translations.literal: This humble servant's nature is weak and inferior; my strength does not match a sturdy woman's, and I have no other talent. Therefore I devoted my mind solely to books, forgetting sleep and food—even dreaming of disputing right and wrong with ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: My nature is weak; I have scarcely the strength of a sturdy woman and no other gifts. So I devoted myself wholly to books, forgetting sleep and food—even dreaming that I debated right and wrong with ghosts.

sentences.zh: 遂得周公、孔子之要術，始知古人有虛有實，妄語者多，真正者少。

translations.literal: I thereby grasped the essential techniques of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, and began to know that among the ancients there were false and true—many who spoke rashly, few who were genuinely correct.
translations.idiomatic: In time I mastered the essential methods of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, and came to see that among the ancients truth and falsehood were mixed—reckless words were many, genuine wisdom was rare.

sentences.zh: 自秦始皇燒書之後，經典絕滅。

translations.literal: Since the Qin First Emperor burned the books, the classics were utterly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since the First Emperor of Qin burned the books, the classics were utterly lost.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖以來，世人妄造曆術者有十餘家，皆不得天道之正，大誤四千，[4]小誤甚多，不可言盡。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Gaozu of Han, more than a dozen men among the world have rashly invented calendrical arts—all failing to attain Heaven's Way correctly; in major matters they err by four thousand [4], in minor matters they err greatly beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of Emperor Gaozu of Han, more than a dozen men have rashly devised calendrical systems—and none has grasped Heaven's Way correctly. Their great errors run to four thousand [4], and their small errors are far too many to recount.

sentences.zh: 臣愍其如此。

translations.literal: This humble servant pities this state of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I lament this state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 今遭陛下太平之世，除偽從真，宜改誤曆，以從天道。

translations.literal: Now we have encountered Your Majesty's age of great peace—discarding the false and following the true. The erroneous calendar ought to be corrected to accord with Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now, under Your Majesty's age of peace, it is time to cast off the false and embrace the true, and to reform the erroneous calendar so that it accords with Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 是以臣前奏造曆，今始成訖。

translations.literal: Therefore this humble servant previously memorialized to create a calendar; now at last it is completed.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I earlier memorialized to create a new calendar, and now at last it is finished.

sentences.zh: 謹以奏呈。

translations.literal: Respectfully I submit it for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit it for Your Majesty's review.

sentences.zh: 唯恩省察，以臣曆術宣示中書博士，然後施用。

translations.literal: I pray only for Your gracious examination—let my calendrical art be displayed to the palace scribes and erudites, and then put into use.
translations.idiomatic: I pray only that Your Majesty will examine it graciously, have my calendrical system shown to the palace erudites, and then put it into use.

sentences.zh: 非但時人，天地鬼神知臣得正，可以益國家萬世之名，過於三皇、五帝矣。

translations.literal: Not only people of the age—Heaven, earth, and ghosts and spirits will know that this humble servant has attained correctness; this can enhance the state's name for ten thousand generations, surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Not only the people of this age—even Heaven, earth, and the spirits will know that I have attained the true Way. This will enhance the glory of the state for ten thousand generations, surpassing even the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 」事在律曆志。

translations.literal: " The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Calendrics and Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Calendrics and Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 真君十一年六月誅浩，清河崔氏無遠近，范陽盧氏、太原郭氏、河東柳氏，皆浩之姻親，盡夷其族。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Zhenjun, Hao was executed. The Cui clan of Qinghe, near and far; the Lu clan of Fanyang; the Guo clan of Taiyuan; the Liu clan of Hedong—all were Hao's affinal kin—and their entire clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Zhenjun, Hao was executed. The Cui clan of Qinghe, near and far; the Lu clan of Fanyang; the Guo clan of Taiyuan; and the Liu clan of Hedong—all Hao's affinal kin—were exterminated to the last member.

sentences.zh: 初，郄標等立石銘刊國記，浩盡述國事，備而不典。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qie Biao and others had erected stone inscriptions to carve the national chronicle; Hao fully narrated state affairs—comprehensive but not canonical in tone.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qie Biao and others erected stone inscriptions to carve the national chronicle, Hao narrated state affairs in full—thorough in detail, but not canonical in tone.

sentences.zh: 而石銘顯在衢路，往來行者咸以為言，事遂聞發。

translations.literal: Yet the stone inscriptions stood conspicuous on the public roads; travelers coming and going all spoke of them, and the matter was thereupon exposed.
translations.idiomatic: But the inscriptions stood in plain view on the public roads, and every traveler had something to say about them—until the matter came to light.

sentences.zh: 有司按驗浩，取祕書郎吏及長曆生數百人意狀。

translations.literal: The responsible officials investigated Hao and took written depositions from several hundred Secretarial clerks and calendrical students.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials investigated Hao and took depositions from several hundred secretarial clerks and calendrical students.

sentences.zh: 浩伏受賕，其祕書郎吏已下盡死。

translations.literal: Hao confessed to accepting bribes; all the Secretarial clerks and those below were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hao confessed to accepting bribes, and all the secretarial clerks and subordinates were put to death.

sentences.zh: 浩始弱冠，太原郭逸以女妻之。

translations.literal: When Hao first reached his weak-crown years, Guo Yi of Taiyuan gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao first came of age, Guo Yi of Taiyuan gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 浩晚成，不曜華采，故時人未知。

translations.literal: Hao matured late and did not display brilliant qualities; therefore people of the age did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was a late bloomer and showed no outward brilliance, so people of the time did not yet recognize his talent.

sentences.zh: 逸妻王氏，劉義隆鎮北將軍王仲德姊也，每奇浩才能，自以為得壻。

translations.literal: Yi's wife, Lady Wang—elder sister of Wang Zhongde, General Who Pacifies the North under Liu Yilong—always marveled at Hao's talent and considered herself to have gained a fine son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's wife, Lady Wang—elder sister of Wang Zhongde, General Who Pacifies the North under Liu Yilong—always admired Hao's gifts and felt she had secured an excellent son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 俄而女亡，王深以傷恨，復以少女繼婚。

translations.literal: Soon the daughter died; Wang was deeply grieved and resentful, and gave her younger daughter in marriage to succeed the first.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the daughter died. Lady Wang was deeply grieved and gave her younger daughter to Hao in a second marriage.

sentences.zh: 逸及親屬以為不可，王固執與之，逸不能違，遂重結好。

translations.literal: Yi and his kin considered it unsuitable, but Wang obstinately insisted on giving her to him; Yi could not refuse, and they thereby renewed the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his relatives thought it unsuitable, but Lady Wang stubbornly insisted; Yi could not refuse, and the two families renewed their alliance.

sentences.zh: 浩非毀佛法，而妻郭氏敬好釋典，時時讀誦。

translations.literal: Hao did not slander the Buddhist Law, yet his wife Lady Guo revered and loved Buddhist scriptures and regularly read and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not himself attack the Buddhist teachings, but his wife Lady Guo revered the Buddhist scriptures and read and recited them regularly.

sentences.zh: 浩怒，取而焚之，捐灰於厠中。

translations.literal: Hao in anger seized them and burned them, casting the ashes into the latrine.
translations.idiomatic: Hao flew into a rage, seized the texts and burned them, and threw the ashes into the latrine.

sentences.zh: 及浩幽執，置之檻內，送於城南，使衞士數十人溲其上，呼聲嗷嗷，聞于行路。

translations.literal: When Hao was secretly imprisoned, he was placed in a cage and sent to the south of the city; several dozen guards were made to urinate on him. His cries were loud and anguished, audible to passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was imprisoned, he was placed in a cage and sent to the south of the city, where several dozen guards were ordered to urinate on him. His cries were loud and agonized, heard by every passerby.

sentences.zh: 自宰司之被戮辱，未有如浩者，世皆以為報應之驗也。

translations.literal: Since ministers have suffered execution and humiliation, none has been like Hao; the world all regarded it as proof of karmic retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Never had a minister suffered execution and humiliation like Hao's; the world took it as proof of karmic retribution.

sentences.zh: 初浩構害李順，基萌已成，夜夢秉火爇順寢室，火作而順死，浩與室家羣立而觀之。

translations.literal: When Hao first framed Li Shun and the foundation of the plot was already laid, he dreamed by night that he held fire and burned Shun's bedchamber; the fire rose and Shun died, while Hao and his household stood together watching.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao first plotted against Li Shun and the scheme was already set, he dreamed one night that he held a torch and set fire to Shun's bedchamber; the flames rose and Shun died, while Hao and his family stood together watching.

sentences.zh: 俄而順弟息號哭而出，曰：「此輩，吾賊也！

translations.literal: Soon Shun's younger brother's son came out wailing, crying: "These people—they are my enemies!
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shun's nephew came out wailing and cried, "These people are my enemies!

sentences.zh: 」以戈擊之，悉投於河。

translations.literal: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.
translations.idiomatic: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.

sentences.zh: 寤而惡之，以告館客馮景仁。

translations.literal: Awakening, he found it ominous and told his house guest Feng Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Waking, he found the dream ominous and told his house guest Feng Jingren.

sentences.zh: 景仁曰：「此真不善也，非復虛事。

translations.literal: Jingren said: "This is truly inauspicious—it is no longer an empty matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren said, "This is truly inauspicious—it is no longer a mere dream.

sentences.zh: 夫以火爇人，暴之極也。

translations.literal: To burn people with fire is the extreme of cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: To burn a man with fire is cruelty in its utmost form.

sentences.zh: 階亂兆禍，復己招也。

translations.literal: A step toward disorder foretokens disaster—you will bring calamity upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: A step toward disorder foretokens disaster—you are bringing calamity upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 商書曰：『惡之易也，如火之燎於原，不可向邇，其猶可撲滅乎？

translations.literal: The Book of Shang says: 'Evil is easy, like fire blazing across a plain—one cannot approach it; can it still be stamped out?'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Shang says, 'Evil spreads easily, like fire blazing across a plain—one cannot approach near; can it still be stamped out?'

sentences.zh: 』且兆始惡者有終殃，積不善者無餘慶。

translations.literal: ' Moreover, those who first foretoken evil meet final calamity; those who accumulate wrongdoing have no surplus of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: ' Moreover, he who first foretokens evil meets final calamity; he who accumulates wrongdoing finds no lasting blessing.

sentences.zh: 厲階成矣，公其圖之。

translations.literal: The stairway to ruin is already built—my lord, consider this.
translations.idiomatic: The stairway to ruin is already built—my lord, you must think on this.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰「吾方思之」，而不能悛，至是而族。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "I am just considering it," yet could not repent—and at this point his clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "I am just considering it," yet could not repent—and in the end his clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 浩既工書，人多託寫急就章。

translations.literal: Hao was skilled at calligraphy; many people entrusted him to copy the Jijiuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was skilled in calligraphy, and many people asked him to copy the Jijiuzhang for them.

sentences.zh: [5]從少至老，初不憚勞，所書蓋以百數，必稱「馮代強」，以示不敢犯國，其謹也如此。

translations.literal: [5] From youth to old age he never shrank from labor; what he wrote surely numbered in the hundreds—and he always signed "Feng Daiqiang," to show he dared not offend against the state. Such was his caution.
translations.idiomatic: [5] From youth to old age he never shrank from labor; his written copies surely numbered in the hundreds—and he always signed them "Feng Daiqiang," to show he dared not use his own name in a way that might offend the state. Such was his caution.

sentences.zh: 浩書體勢及其先人，而妙巧不如也。

translations.literal: Hao's calligraphic structure and momentum matched his forebears, yet in subtle mastery he did not equal them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's calligraphic structure and force matched his forebears', yet in subtle elegance he fell short of them.

sentences.zh: 世寶其迹，多裁割綴連以為模楷。

translations.literal: The age treasured his traces; many cut and spliced them together to serve as models.
translations.idiomatic: The age treasured his hand; many trimmed and joined his strokes together to serve as models.

sentences.zh: 浩母盧氏，諶孫也。

translations.literal: Hao's mother, Lady Lu, was a granddaughter of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's mother, Lady Lu, was a granddaughter of Shen.

sentences.zh: 浩著食經敍曰：「余自少及長，耳目聞見，諸母諸姑所修婦功，無不蘊習酒食。

translations.literal: Hao wrote a preface to the Classic of Food saying: "From my youth to my maturity, all that my ears heard and my eyes saw—the domestic crafts of my various aunts and elder female kin in preparing food and drink—none was I not thoroughly steeped in.
translations.idiomatic: In the preface to his Classic of Food, Hao wrote: "From youth to maturity, everything my ears heard and my eyes saw—the domestic crafts my aunts and elder female kin practiced in preparing food and drink—I was thoroughly steeped in them all.

sentences.zh: 朝夕養舅姑，四時祭祀，雖有功力，不任僮使，常手自親焉。

translations.literal: Morning and evening I cared for my parents-in-law; at the four seasons' sacrifices—though there was labor enough—I did not leave it to servants and slaves, but always attended with my own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening I cared for my parents-in-law; at the sacrifices of the four seasons—though the labor was great—I did not delegate it to servants but always did it with my own hands.

sentences.zh: 昔遭喪亂，飢饉仍臻，饘蔬餬口，不能具其物用，十餘年間不復備設。

translations.literal: In the past we suffered turmoil and disorder; famine followed in succession—we subsisted on gruel and vegetables and could not provide the full array of items; for more than ten years the full setup was not restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the past we lived through chaos and famine followed in succession—we subsisted on gruel and vegetables and could not provide the full array of offerings; for more than ten years the full ceremonial spread was not restored.

sentences.zh: 先妣慮久廢忘，後生無知見，而少不習業書，乃占授為九篇，文辭約舉，婉而成章，聰辯強記，皆此類也。

translations.literal: My late mother feared long neglect and forgetting, and that later generations would have no knowledge; as I was young and had not studied written arts, she dictated and instructed nine chapters—the prose concise and well-chosen, graceful and formed into chapters; keen in speech and strong in memory—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: My late mother feared these arts would be forgotten, and that later generations would know nothing of them; as I was young and had not studied letters, she dictated and taught me nine chapters—the prose concise and well-chosen, graceful and formed as chapters; keen in speech and strong in memory—all her gifts were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 親沒之後，值國龍興之會，平暴除亂，拓定四方。

translations.literal: After my parents died, we met the era when the state arose like a dragon—pacifying violence and purging disorder, expanding and settling the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After my parents died, the state rose like a dragon—pacifying violence, purging disorder, and securing the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 余備位台鉉，與參大謀，賞獲豐厚，牛羊蓋澤，貲累巨萬。

translations.literal: I occupy a place among the highest ministers and participate in great counsels; rewards have been ample—cattle and sheep cover the marshes, and my accumulated wealth reaches tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: I hold high office and share in great counsels; my rewards have been ample—cattle and sheep cover the marshlands, and my accumulated wealth runs to vast sums.

sentences.zh: 衣則重錦，食則粱肉。

translations.literal: For clothing, heavy brocade; for food, fine millet and meat.
translations.idiomatic: I wear heavy brocade and eat fine grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 遠惟平生，思季路負米之時，不可復得，故序遺文，垂示來世。」

translations.literal: Looking back across my whole life, I think of the time when Jilu carried rice on his back—that cannot be recovered. Therefore I set forth these surviving texts to be handed down to later ages."
translations.idiomatic: Looking back across my life, I think of the time when Zilu carried rice on his back—that cannot be recovered. So I set forth these surviving texts to be handed down to later ages."

sentences.zh: 始浩與冀州刺史賾、滎陽太守模等年皆相次，浩為長，次模，次賾。

translations.literal: From the first Hao, Ze the Inspector of Ji Province, Mo the Administrator of Xingyang, and the rest were all close in age—Hao was eldest, next Mo, next Ze.
translations.idiomatic: From the start, Hao, Ze the Inspector of Ji Province, Mo the Administrator of Xingyang, and the rest were close in age—Hao was eldest, then Mo, then Ze.

sentences.zh: 三人別祖，而模、賾為親。

translations.literal: The three traced to different founding ancestors, yet Mo and Ze were kin.
translations.idiomatic: The three traced to different founding ancestors, but Mo and Ze were kin.

sentences.zh: 浩恃其家世魏晉公卿，常侮模、賾。

translations.literal: Hao relied on his family's descent from Wei-Jin high ministers and often insulted Mo and Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, relying on his family's descent from Wei and Jin high ministers, often looked down on Mo and Ze.

sentences.zh: 模謂人曰：「桃簡正可欺我，何合輕我家周兒也。

translations.literal: Mo said to someone: "Taojian may just bully me—why should he also slight my family's Zhou'er?
translations.idiomatic: Mo said to someone, "Taojian may bully me as he likes—but why should he slight my family's Zhou'er as well?

sentences.zh: 」浩小名桃簡，賾小名周兒。

translations.literal: " Hao's childhood name was Taojian; Ze's childhood name was Zhou'er.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao's childhood name was Taojian; Ze's childhood name was Zhou'er.

sentences.zh: 世祖頗聞之，故誅浩時，二家獲免。

translations.literal: Shizu had heard quite a bit of this; therefore when Hao was executed, the two families were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had heard of this, and so when Hao was executed, the two families were spared.

sentences.zh: 浩既不信佛、道，模深所歸向，每雖糞土之中，禮拜形像。

translations.literal: Hao did not believe in Buddhism or Daoism; Mo deeply devoted himself to them—even in filth and dust he would bow before images.
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not believe in Buddhism or Daoism, but Mo was deeply devoted to them—even in filth and dust he would bow before images.

sentences.zh: 浩大笑之，云：「持此頭顱不淨處跪是胡神也。」

translations.literal: Hao loudly laughed at him, saying: "To hold this head of yours and kneel in an unclean place before some barbarian god!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao laughed at him and said, "To hold this head of yours and kneel in filth before some barbarian god!"

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔浩才藝通博，究覽天人，政事籌策，時莫之二，此其所以自比於子房也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Cui Hao's talent and learning were comprehensive and broad; he exhaustively surveyed Heaven and human affairs; in government planning and stratagem none of the age could compare with him—this was why he likened himself to Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cui Hao's talent and learning were vast; he mastered Heaven and human affairs alike; in statecraft and strategy none of his age could rival him—hence his comparison of himself to Zifang.

sentences.zh: 屬太宗為政之秋，值世祖經營之日，言聽計從，寧廓區夏。

translations.literal: He fell in the autumn of Taizong's governance, in the days when Shizu was building the realm—his words were heeded and his plans followed, and the Central Plains were pacified and settled.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the autumn of Emperor Taizong's reign and through the days when the Emperor built the realm—his counsel was heard and followed, and the Central Plains were pacified.

sentences.zh: 遇既隆也，勤亦茂哉。

translations.literal: His favor was already lofty; his diligence was likewise abundant!
translations.idiomatic: His favor was already lofty—and his diligence was abundant indeed.

sentences.zh: 謀雖蓋世，威未震主，末途邂逅，遂不自全。

translations.literal: Though his stratagems covered the age, his authority did not overawe his lord; at the end of the road he met with mischance and could not preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though his stratagems covered the age, his authority never overawed his lord; at the end he met with mischance and could not save himself.

sentences.zh: 豈鳥盡弓藏，民惡其上？

translations.literal: Was it that when the birds are gone the bow is stored away—that the people hate those above them?
translations.idiomatic: Was it that when the birds are gone the bow is put away—that the people hate those above them?

sentences.zh: 將器盈必概，陰害貽禍？

translations.literal: Or that when the vessel overflows it must be levelled—that secret harm brings down disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Or that when the vessel overflows the water must be skimmed—that secret harm brings down disaster?

sentences.zh: 何斯人而遭斯酷，悲夫！

translations.literal: Why should such a man meet such cruel fate? Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Why should such a man suffer such a cruel fate? Alas!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 乃徐徐西遁 諸本「西」作「四」，北史卷二一作「西」。

translations.literal: "Then slowly fled west"—in all editions "west" (西) is written as "four" (四); Beishi juan 21 has "west."
translations.idiomatic: "Then slowly fled west": every edition writes west (西) as four (四); Beishi juan 21 has west.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑卷一二一

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian juan 121
translations.idiomatic: According to Zizhi Tongjian juan 121

sentences.zh: 〈三八一二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3812〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 3812〉

sentences.zh: 也作「西」。

translations.literal: also has "west."
translations.idiomatic: also reads "west."

sentences.zh: 卷四上世祖紀上神䴥二年五月丁未、卷一０三蠕蠕傳補記此事並云「絕跡西走」。

translations.literal: Juan 4A, Basic Annals of Shizu A, second year of Shengui, fifth month, day dingwei; and juan 103, Biography of the Rouran, supplementary record of this event—all say "vanished without trace fleeing west."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 4A (Basic Annals of Shizu), second year of Shengui, fifth month, day dingwei, and juan 103 (Biography of the Rouran), which supplementally record this event, all read "vanished without trace fleeing west."

sentences.zh: 「四」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "four" is erroneous; it is now emended according to [the other sources].
translations.idiomatic: The character four is erroneous; the text is now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至於姑臧城南 北史卷二一崔宏附崔浩傳此句作「至於涼州，地純枯石，了無水草，不見流川。

translations.literal: "As for south of Guzang city"—Beishi juan 21, Biography of Cui Hong with appended Biography of Cui Hao, has this sentence as "As for Liang Province—the land is wholly dry stone, utterly without water or grass; no flowing streams are seen.
translations.idiomatic: "As for south of Guzang city": Beishi juan 21 (Cui Hong with appended Cui Hao) reads this sentence as "As for Liang Province—the land is wholly dry stone, utterly without water or grass; no flowing streams are seen.

sentences.zh: 又言姑臧城南」，「至於」下多出十六字。

translations.literal: Then it again says "south of Guzang city";"—under "as for" sixteen characters are added.
translations.idiomatic: Then again "south of Guzang city";"—sixteen extra characters appear after "as for."

sentences.zh: 按無此十六字，語意不全，當是本書傳本脫去。

translations.literal: According to examination, without these sixteen characters the sense is incomplete; they were surely lost through defection in the transmitted text of this book.
translations.idiomatic: Without these sixteen characters the sense is incomplete; they were surely lost in the transmitted text of this book.

sentences.zh: 一日之內未便損傷 北史卷二一「內」作「乏」。

translations.literal: "Within a single day one would not yet suffer harm"—Beishi juan 21 has "内" written as "乏" (want/scarcity).
translations.idiomatic: "Within a single day one would not yet suffer harm": Beishi juan 21 writes 内 (within) as 乏 (scarcity).

sentences.zh: 按上文說「渭北地空，穀草不滿」，所以拓跋燾不想走北道，這裏是說從北道往只一天路程，還長安也止一天，一天的糧食匱乏，不致受損害。

translations.literal: According to examination, the passage above says "north of the Wei the land is empty, grain and grass do not fill it"; therefore Tuoba Tao did not wish to take the northern route. Here it says that from the northern route it is only one day's journey—and to Chang'an also only one day; one day's scarcity of provisions would not cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: The passage above says "north of the Wei the land is empty and grain and grass insufficient," explaining why Tuoba Tao did not wish to take the northern route. Here the point is that the northern route is only one day's march—and Chang'an is also only one day away; a single day's scarcity of provisions would not cause serious harm.

sentences.zh: 作「乏」較長。

translations.literal: Writing "scarcity" (乏) is preferable.
translations.idiomatic: Reading scarcity (乏) is preferable.

sentences.zh: 大誤四千 李慈銘云：「四千當作四十。」

translations.literal: "Great errors of four thousand"—Li Ciming says: "Four thousand should read forty."
translations.idiomatic: "Great errors of four thousand": Li Ciming says four thousand should read forty.

sentences.zh: 人多託寫急就章 諸本「人」上有「蓋」字，北史卷二一無。

translations.literal: "Many people entrusted him to copy the Jijiuzhang"—in all editions above "people" there is the character "盖"; Beishi juan 21 lacks it.
translations.idiomatic: "Many people entrusted him to copy the Jijiuzhang": every edition has the character 盖 before "people"; Beishi juan 21 lacks it.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「與下文『蓋』字行次適並，因而致誤。

translations.literal: Li Ciming says: "The line order coincides with the "盖" character below, causing the error.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming says, "Its line position coincided with the 盖 character below, producing the error.

sentences.zh: 」按文義不當有此字，今據北史刪。

translations.literal: " According to examination, the sense does not permit this character; it is now deleted according to Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: " According to the sense the character does not belong; it is now deleted following Beishi.
